items.title: Govt, opposition begin second round of talks ahead of PTI's Islamabad march
items.description: Delegations from the government and the opposition began a second round of talks on Saturday afternoon to discuss various issues, including the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. The meeting, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, is aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. It comes ahead of the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government. As the huddle began, the NA speaker expressed his hope that the talks would proceed in the same “cordial atmosphere” as Friday’s, according to a post on the NA’s X account. The government side includes minister for frontier regions Amir Muqam, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry. Senator Sherry Rehman, along with MNAs Syed Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Hussain Jakhrani, is representing the PPP. The opposition delegation comprises Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, PTI interim chairman MNA Gohar Ali Khan, Opposition Chief Whip Amir Dogar, MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh. KP CM adamant on long march Earlier in the day, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi voiced his determination to hold the long march on Oct 4 and vowed to prevent a repeat of the events of May 9, 2023. In response, Chaudhry said the KP CM’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process and urged PTI leaders not to engage in such discourse. In his post, CM Afridi said PTI was the largest and most popular political party in Pakistan. “Pakistan is a democratic country whose Constitution grants us the right to peaceful protest.” Detailing his long march plan, Afridi said an “ocean of people” would begin its journey from Gandi Chowk in Lakki Marwat at 1pm on Oct 4. The party would continue its struggle until the supremacy of the Constitution and the law was ensured in Pakistan and an independent judiciary was restored, the PTI leader added. “All demands of the PTI are in accordance with the constitution and the law.” In his post, he stressed that the party would “neither allow May 9 to happen again nor allow anyone else to repeat it”. Reacting to the KP CM’s remarks, Chaudhry said Afridi’s statements could affect the ongoing negotiation process even though the government wanted them to be “meaningful and fruitful”. He urged PTI leaders to refrain from making such statements until the final stage of the negotiations, so that the dialogue process was not “harmed”. “The language that Sohail Afridi is using against his opponents and our leadership does not seem like that of a chief minister; his statements are extremely indecent and reprehensible,” Chaudhry said. Speaking to reporters ahead of the meeting, PPP’s Rehman stressed that her party was making efforts to solve issues in a democratic manner. Asked about KP CM being adamant on the PTI march, the PPP leader said it was up to the PTI, but added that she would refrain from making comments before the talks conclude. While acknowledging that each party had its positions, she noted that the objective of holding negotiations was to “discuss those positions”. Opposition decides SOPs Earlier in the day, the opposition held a meeting in which standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the talks were finalised. It was decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one from either side would speak to the media during the talks and that a joint statement would be issued afterwards to avoid any misunderstanding. Talking to Dawn , TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai said comments made by PPP leader Sherry Rehman on Friday had triggered a controversy, leaving the situation unpleasant until late at night. “The opposition alliance held a meeting before the start of the talks, during which the government side’s views regarding the law and order situation in KP were discussed. After consultation with the KP chief minister, a response was prepared, which will be presented to the government side during the meeting today,” he said. Replying to a question, Akhunzada said it was also decided that it would be proposed during the meeting that no one would issue a media statement regarding the dialogue and that a joint statement would be issued after the meeting. He said the joint statement would reduce chances of confusion and differences of opinion. ‘Political solutions to political problems’ In a post on X a day earlier, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, an ally of the PML-N government, pressed PTI to unconditionally call off the long march, which, he said, would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and threats emanating from neighbouring countries. Bilawal also welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”. On Friday, PTI KP Secretary Information Shaukat Yousafzai said that the party’s protest march would start from the southern districts and be led by CM Afridi. “The march on October 4 will take place at any cost,” he said in a statement. Also on Friday, the army’s top brass warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”. The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. “[The] forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create [a] May 9-like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination,” a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. For the first time in almost three years, representatives of the federal government and the opposition PTI formally came together on Friday for talks aimed at easing the political tension in the country, and apprised each other of their positions. Though neither side shared its specific demands with the media, both were hopeful of a positive outcome from the meeting. Sources on both sides told Dawn that the PTI wants its incarcerated founder Imran Khan to be shifted from jail to a hospital for medical treatment, while the government has insisted that the opposition call off its protest march on Islamabad. In August, PTI announced a long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of Imran. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4. Emergency option The talks come as the PTI remains resolute on the march. Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while the PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step is taken. The decision to hold talks was taken on Thursday at a presidency meeting attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Mr Naqvi, Attorney General Mansoor Awan and other PPP and PML-N leaders. A source privy to the huddle told Dawn the emergency option was discussed, but participants agreed to first give the opposition a chance to settle matters peacefully through dialogue, and to seriously consider an emergency only if the PTI did not back down. The coalition also believes the march will remain confined to KP and not enter Punjab or Islamabad. On Thursday, Sanaullah said the government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” over the protest, and that the decision on the march rested with the PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”. “So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned. Separately, the prime minister has invited Achakzai for dialogue, and the two are expected to meet in the coming days.

items.title: Reacciones a los decretos de vivienda y las acampadas en directo | Una marcha masiva llega a Cibeles para exigir vivienda y llama a una huelga general “gobierne quien gobierne”
items.description: El Sindicato de Inquilinas ha vuelto a llamar a la movilización este sábado después de que el voto en contra de PP, Vox y Junts tumbara los dos decretos con medidas sobre vivienda impulsados por el Gobierno. Hay convocadas unas 50 movilizaciones en ciudades de toda España bajo el lema “Hacia la huelga general”. En Madrid, la movilización ha arrancado a las 12 con cuatro columnas formadas por miles de personas que han confluido en Cibeles. La portavoz del sindicato de inquilinas, Valeria Racu, ha insistido desde Atocha en que el camino del movimiento es la huelga general, aunque sin dar una fecha concreta. Racu solo ha dicho que se convocará “pronto” y que lo hará “junto a los sindicatos laborales”, con quienes mantiene conversaciones y que la convocarán “gobierne quien gobierne”. “Ocho días de poder popular han hecho mucho más que ocho años de Gobierno progresista”, ha añadido Racu. En Valencia, la manifestación ha terminado con altercados entre los manifestantes y la policía, que ha acabado lanzando botes de gas lacrimógeno para disolver la protesta y pelotas de goma al aire. Un grupo de manifestantes ha sobrepasado el cordón de vallas que rodeaba el Palau de las Artes de Valencia, donde tiene lugar un foro de inversión inmobiliaria, y algunos han logrado acceder al edificio. items.title: L’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies: Le ROJALNU mondial reçu par la Sous-secrétaire générale des Nations Unies
items.description: En marge de la 81ᵉ session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, Diene Keita, Sous-secrétaire générale des Nations Unies et Directrice exécutive du Fonds des Nations Unies pour la population (UNFPA), a reçu le jeudi 1 er octobre dernier une délégation du Réseau des Organisations des Jeunes Leaders des Nations Unies (ROJALNU Mondial), conduite par son Président mondial, le Burkinabè Abraham Zida Bila. La rencontre a eu pour cadre le siège de l’UNFPA à New York. Au cours de l’audience, madame Keita a adressé ses encouragements à la jeunesse mondiale à travers le ROJALNU mondial et salué les initiatives visant à promouvoir une participation citoyenne, responsable et constructive des jeunes. Elle a réaffirmé l’importance de placer la jeunesse au cœur des réflexions et des actions en faveur de la paix, de la sécurité, du développement durable et de la cohésion sociale. Au nom du ROJALNU mondial, son président, Abraham Zida Bila, a exprimé sa profonde gratitude à la Sous-secrétaire générale des Nations Unies pour sa disponibilité, son écoute et l’attention accordée à la délégation. Il a salué son engagement en faveur d’une participation plus inclusive et significative de la jeunesse dans les espaces de dialogue et de décision aux niveaux national, régional et international. Evoquant la dynamique engagée au Burkina Faso, le Président mondial du ROJALNU a salué l’attention accordée à la jeunesse par le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré Président du Faso, ainsi que les opportunités offertes aux jeunes pour contribuer pleinement à la vie de la Nation et qui reste une vitrine pleinement profitable au Colloque Mondial. Abraham Zida Bila a réaffirmé l’engagement de l’organisation à faire du prochain Colloque mondial de la jeunesse un véritable cadre de réflexion, de dialogue et surtout d’action au service de la jeunesse mondiale. Yves OUEDRAOGO

items.title: Latest Ranking: 10 best universities in Africa
items.description: The University of Cape Town (UCT) has emerged as Africa’s highest-ranked university in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, with the continent showing broader representation in the latest global assessment. UCT placed joint 147th in the world, improving from its joint 164th position in the previous edition, as universities across Africa continued to gain visibility in international higher education. The latest ranking features 69 universities from sub-Saharan Africa, compared with 55 in the previous edition. South Africa dominated the African list, accounting for most of the continent’s highest-ranked institutions. Universities from Morocco and Egypt also secured places among Africa’s leading institutions. For the 2027 edition, Times Higher Education evaluated 2,297 universities in 118 countries and territories, making it the largest ranking exercise conducted by the organisation. The ranking considers a range of measures, including teaching, research, research quality, industry engagement and international outlook. Below are the 10 best-ranked universities in Africa in the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings. 1. University of Cape Town — South Africa The University of Cape Town retained the top position in Africa, ranking joint 147th globally with an overall score of 62.4. Founded in 1829, UCT is based in Cape Town and is among the oldest universities on the continent. Its academic structure comprises six faculties: Commerce, Engineering and the Built Environment, Health Sciences, Humanities, Law and Science. UCT has 20,318 students, with women accounting for 57% and men 43%. International students make up 13% of the university’s total student population. 2. University of the Witwatersrand — South Africa The University of the Witwatersrand, widely known as Wits, occupies the 301–325 bracket globally, recording an overall score between 53.4 and 54.8. The institution traces its origins to the South African School of Mines, founded in Kimberley in 1896. It relocated to Johannesburg in 1904 before attaining full university status in 1922. Wits has 26,766 students, comprising 61% women and 39% men. International students represent 5% of the population, while its student-to-staff ratio stands at 21.6:1. 3. Stellenbosch University — South Africa Stellenbosch University ranks between 326th and 350th globally, with an overall score ranging from 52.3 to 53.3. The institution began in 1918 with four faculties — Arts, Science, Education and Agriculture — and had 503 students and 40 lecturers at the time. It has since expanded into a major institution operating across five campuses and 10 faculties. The university has 27,676 students, with women representing 57% and men 43%. International students account for 7% of the student body. 4. University of Johannesburg — South Africa The University of Johannesburg is placed in the 351–375 global range, posting an overall score of between 51.6 and 52.2. The public university was established in 2005 following the merger of Rand Afrikaans University, Technikon Witwatersrand and parts of Vista University. Since its creation, the institution has developed a strong profile in research, innovation and international partnerships. The University of Johannesburg has 33,530 students, of whom 57% are women and 43% are men. International students constitute 13% of the student population. 5. Mohammed VI Polytechnic University — Morocco Morocco’s Mohammed VI Polytechnic University is ranked 376–400 globally, with a score ranging from 50.5 to 51.5. Established in 2016, the university forms part of the Green City project initiated by King Mohammed VI in 2009, with an emphasis on sustainable development, research and education. The institution has 2,650 students, including 56% women and 44% men. International students make up 7% of the student population, while the student-to-staff ratio is 7:1. 6. University of Pretoria — South Africa The University of Pretoria falls within the 451–500 bracket worldwide, recording an overall score of 47.4–48.7. The South African university has nine faculties and a business school and places considerable emphasis on research and its wider impact. items.title: France and Ghana’s Gender Ministry explore cooperation on women’s economic empowerment
items.description: The French Embassy in Ghana and the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection have begun discussions to strengthen cooperation on women’s economic empowerment, focusing on entrepreneurship, agriculture and gender-responsive development. The Ambassador of France to Ghana, Diarra Dime-Labille, led a delegation to the Ministry for a courtesy call on the Minister, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, where both sides explored areas for collaboration. The Ambassador said the engagement aimed to deepen the longstanding relationship between France and Ghana while identifying opportunities for French support to complement the Ministry’s priorities. She identified women’s entrepreneurship and agriculture as areas with strong potential for cooperation, particularly in promoting innovation, food security and economic opportunities for women. She also expressed interest in ongoing initiatives supporting women entrepreneurs and how future programmes could better integrate gender considerations. Dr Lartey welcomed the engagement and stressed the need for gender to be deliberately placed at the centre of programmes designed to empower women economically. She noted that although gender is a cross-cutting issue, concerns affecting women can sometimes be overshadowed by broader sector priorities, particularly in agriculture where women have historically played significant roles, often informally. The Minister said Ghana’s transition towards more formalised and technology-driven agricultural systems must not leave women behind, adding that the Ministry was ready to work with the French Embassy to ensure investments in women-focused initiatives deliver sustainable results. She also urged the Embassy to involve the Ministry from the planning stage of programmes with gender dimensions, citing the proposed 2027 Women Economic Empowerment Programme as a potential area for collaboration. Dr Lartey further encouraged the French delegation to share relevant gender action plans and programme documents with the Ministry to ensure alignment with Ghana’s national priorities. She pointed to the National Gender Policy as a key framework for guiding interventions and said the Ministry could support public institutions and local-level structures in developing and implementing gender plans while monitoring progress through established reporting mechanisms. Both sides expressed interest in identifying practical areas of cooperation and strengthening the partnership to expand opportunities for women and advance gender equality in Ghana.

items.title: Ghana’s growing drug trafficking links are deeply troubling – Victoria Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer and entrepreneur says the growing number of drug trafficking cases linked to Ghana is deeply troubling and requires urgent national attention. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile, she said the scale and frequency of recent seizures suggest that Ghana’s involvement in international drug trafficking may extend beyond isolated incidents. “The scale and the frequency of these recent seizures, well in the last year, linked to Ghana, are extremely troubling,” she said. Ms Bright said the consignments have been detected through different channels, including commercial containers, road transport and passenger aviation, with some of the largest shipments intercepted after leaving Ghana. She cited figures from a German research analyst indicating that 28 drug busts were recorded between March 2025 and September 2026, 11 of which involved cocaine. According to the figures she referenced, about 16 tonnes of Ghana-linked cocaine, with an estimated street value of $1.3 billion to $1.7 billion, were intercepted during the period. Ms Bright said the figures are particularly concerning because Ghana does not produce cocaine. “We don’t produce cocaine in this country, and those cocaine figures are particularly striking.” She said seven of the 11 cocaine seizures were made in Ghana, while four were intercepted abroad. By weight, she said approximately 3.6 tonnes were intercepted in Ghana compared with about 4.4 tonnes intercepted in Europe, raising questions about the quantity of drugs that may be passing through the country undetected. Ms Bright also cited several methods allegedly used to conceal the drugs, including consignments hidden beneath sand in a cement truck at Cape Coast, inside wood shipments bound for Europe and in cassava flour. She said the emerging pattern should compel authorities to investigate the broader networks behind the trade. “This is something that should command our utmost attention.”

items.title: North Korea says test of intermediate-range strategic missile included use of AI
items.description: North Korea said it tested an intermediate-range strategic missile on Saturday that involved the use of AI, hours after Seoul said Pyongyang had launched a ballistic missile. The launch took place days after Seoul’s military demanded an apology from Pyongyang for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) that it blamed on the North. Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue. Early on Saturday, “our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea,” Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan. “South Korea, the US, and Japan are maintaining a robust defence posture through close information sharing regarding North Korean ballistic missiles,” it said, adding the missile flew more than 700 kilometres. Hours later, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of Pyongyang’s leader Kim Jong Un, said the missile fired in the morning was an “intermediate-range strategic missile”. She said the projectile is “capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude and AI was introduced into it”, without elaborating further on the use of artificial intelligence. She said it meant “there is no way to avoid” the missile’s attack, and claimed Kim Jong Un believed “any country in the world could not have access to such technology for at least several years”. Her latest statement followed Kim Jong Un’s remarks last month stressing the need to raise “the level of artificial intelligence” in the country’s weapons systems. Kim Yo Jong claimed that whenever North Korea “applied the wave-like trajectory mode”, South Korea “failed to track the targets from their first skip points”. Analysts say North Korea could be rapidly advancing its missile technology with Russian military support in exchange for sending troops to support its war against Ukraine. “AI is increasingly being incorporated into military technology worldwide, and ballistic missiles are no exception,” Hong Sung-pyo, senior researcher at the Seoul-based Korea Institute for Military Affairs, told AFP . “AI can assist with target information and launch operations, while the wars in Ukraine and Iran have shown how linking AI with drones and missiles can enhance their operational effectiveness.” Hong said it was too early to conclude North Korea’s claims about the missile’s capabilities were accurate. “North Korea’s missile technology is not particularly advanced compared with leading military powers,” he said. “While missiles that manoeuvre in their terminal phase are difficult to intercept, that does not mean they can strike their targets with perfect accuracy.” ‘Despicable’ Seoul and the US-led United Nations Command found that last month’s explosion inside the DMZ was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South side of the border. North Korea’s military has placed mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off following leader Kim Jong Un’s designation of South Korea as his country’s “ principal enemy ” in 2024. The mines responsible for the blast, which left three soldiers wounded, were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defence minister Kang Shin-chul. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier. Kim Yo Jong responded by calling Seoul “really despicable” on Friday and once again denied Pyongyang was behind the blasts. She ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch” and said the military’s demand that her country apologise was “quite ridiculous”. Kim also warned Pyongyang was “ready for everything” Seoul might do over the mine blast — remarks followed the next morning by Pyongyang’s missile launch. Analysts said the launch would be viewed as a show of force in response to the South Korean government’s diplomatic efforts, effectively rejecting engagement. “Seoul called for easing tensions, but Pyongyang answered by escalating them,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP . “The message is that the North is pursuing … confrontation in response to goodwill.”

Protección Civil tiene previsto comparecer este mediodía para detallar las medidas, mientras que Illa presidirá por la tarde una reunión de seguimiento del plan Inuncat en la sala Cecat de Interior. El impacto máximo del episodio meteorológico se alcanzará esta medianoche. Durante las próximas 24 horas se esperan lluvias “torrenciales” de 40 mm en media hora. El litoral de Tarragona, Barcelona y Girona son las zonas con mayor amenaza y el Govern prevé restricciones de movilidad a partir de las 20 horas de este sábado hasta las 14 del domingo. ‘The MP’s tears are crocodile tears’ – Kofi Bentil on La Pleasure Beach demolition
items.description: Lawyer and Senior Vice President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has questioned the response of the Member of Parliament for the La Dade-Kotopon constituency to the demolition of structures at the Labadi beachfront, saying her position raises serious questions about how the area is being managed. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 3, Mr Bentil said he found it difficult to understand how the MP, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, who also serves as a Deputy Minister of Local Government, could claim not to have known about an issue reportedly affecting the livelihoods of about 5,000 people in her constituency. “The MP’s tears are crocodile tears,” Mr Bentil said. He said that the MP should have been aware of developments in her constituency, particularly given her position within the Local Government Ministry. “She’s supposed to be in the Local Government Ministry. How do you not know?” he asked. Mr Bentil said the situation raised questions about either the MP’s competence or whether there had been a serious failure to act. “It’s either incompetence or criminal negligence,” he said. Read also: ‘Government has no knowledge’ – La MP questions Labadi Beach demolition Mr Bentil said he was particularly concerned that a senior government official and the MP for the area could both claim not to have known about an issue of such significance. “I think that’s possible. Well, that’s the point I’m making,” he said. “The point I’m making is that if you are a Deputy Minister of Local Government, you are the MP of the area, and something like this affecting 5,000 reportedly of your people, and you don’t know, something terrible is happening.” He questioned who was ultimately responsible for decisions affecting the Labadi area, saying the circumstances had led to wider speculation about who was exercising authority. “My problem is, who is running this town?” he asked. Mr Bentil said he was not convinced that President John Mahama had personally authorised the demolition, pointing to what he described as a disconnect between the action and the President’s character. “There were rumours that, oh, it’s not the President who’s running the country, and so other people are running the country,” he said. “And I say that with due respect to the President, because I don’t see President Mahama’s character in this thing.” “I don’t see President Mahama authorising this,” he added. Mr Bentil also challenged the basis for extending a dispute involving the Labadi area’s Polo Club to the wider Labadi beachfront. He said the dispute, as he understood it, was between two parties and questioned how that could justify action affecting a much larger area. “We were aware, everybody was aware, that the Polo Club issue had to do with a dispute between two parties, Labadi Hotel and the owners of Polo Club, period,” he said. “How does that stretch to the rest of the Labadi Beach?” “Labadi Beach as a tourist enclave, a place, was there years before Labadi Pleasure Beach was built.” He therefore questioned how a dispute over what he described as a small piece of land could result in the destruction of businesses and livelihoods across the wider area. “So how does the dispute between two parties over a small piece of land stretch to destroying the livelihoods of 5,000 people?” he asked.

items.title: Un fonds d’entrepreneuriat à SWISS UMEF Dakar (Par le Professeur Djawed Sangdel)
items.description: Chaque année, des milliers de jeunes diplômés sénégalais quittent les amphithéâtres avec un diplôme en poche et la même question : où trouver un emploi ? L’université SWISS UMEF – Campus de Dakar a choisi de poser la question autrement et si l'étudiant créait lui-même son emploi, et peut-être celui des autres ? C'est l'objet du nouveau Centre de soutien à l'entrepreneuriat étudiant, un dispositif qui entre en vigueur avec l'année académique 2026-2027. Pour cette première année, l'établissement annonce une enveloppe de 180 millions de FCFA. Un prêt à taux zéro, sans caution Le principe est simple : un étudiant porteur d'une idée sérieuse peut obtenir un prêt sans intérêt, plafonné à 3 000 000 F CFA par projet. Le règlement n'exige ni hypothèque ni caution, l'obstacle qui ferme souvent aux jeunes les portes des banques. Le remboursement peut s'étaler sur cinq ans au maximum, selon le montant, la nature du projet et sa maturité. Le dispositif ne s'arrête pas à la remise du diplôme. Les étudiants régulièrement inscrits peuvent postuler, mais aussi les diplômés du campus, pendant trois ans après l'obtention de leur titre. Une manière de reconnaître qu'une entreprise naît rarement le jour de la soutenance. Les projets attendus sont larges : entrepreneuriaux, innovants, sociaux, économiques, culturels ou technologiques. Seule exigence : qu'ils soient « sérieux, structurés, réalistes ». Outre le prêt, le Centre peut proposer un accompagnement, du mentorat, une aide financière ou une avance. D'où vient l'argent Le fonds repose sur un financement partagé. Chaque étudiant y verse obligatoirement 5 000 F CFA par mois, et l'université ajoute 10 000 F CFA par étudiant et par mois. Au total, 15 000 F CFA par étudiant alimentent chaque mois la caisse commune. Le fonds reste ouvert aux dons de partenaires, d'entreprises, d'anciens élèves ou de particuliers. Les étudiants peuvent aussi organiser des collectes, avec l'autorisation de l'établissement. Rendre ce que l'on a reçu La dernière clause donne au dispositif sa logique de chaîne. Une fois son prêt remboursé, l'entrepreneur dont le projet a réussi continue de verser 10 000 F CFA par mois au fonds, pendant au moins cinq ans. Soit 120 000 F CFA par an, pour financer à leur tour les projets des promotions suivantes. Créer son emploi plutôt que l'attendre L'initiative s'inscrit dans un débat récurrent au Sénégal : l'insertion professionnelle d'une jeunesse de plus en plus diplômée. Pour l'établissement, l'université ne doit plus seulement délivrer des diplômes, mais aussi donner les moyens de passer de l'idée à l'activité. Reste à voir combien de projets verront le jour. Avec un plafond de 3 millions de F CFA, l'enveloppe de la première année permettrait de financer une soixantaine de projets au montant maximal et davantage si les prêts accordés sont plus modestes. Professeur Djawed Sangdel Directeur général, Swiss University UMEF

items.title: Freddie Blay alleges Mahama ordered demolition of son’s Polo Beach Club at La Beach
items.description: Former Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Freddie Blay, has accused President John Dramani Mahama of ordering the demolition of his son’s Polo Beach Club at the La Beach enclave in Accra. Mr Blay alleged that the President personally directed the demolition despite an ongoing court dispute over the property. During the NPP’s National Delegates Congress on Saturday, October 3, he said the development was one of the issues he believed should be raised against the government. “I feel sorry. It is one of the complaints that I think people should hear against the NDC government and against President John Mahama, that he himself ordered it. I know,” he said. Mr Blay argued that the demolition was inappropriate because the ownership dispute involving the property had not yet been determined by the court. “The court is yet to determine it. Then you complain to the President and the President orders that they should go and break it. He [Mahama] has no respect for law,” he alleged. According to Mr Blay, the dispute involving his son’s business and the Labadi Beach Hotel has been before the court for about two to three years without a final determination. He rejected suggestions that the Polo Beach Club was operating as a squatter on land belonging to the hotel. “My son has acquired land from the La Stool and did business on the land that belongs to the La Stool originally. They’ve leased it out. And we are working on it,” he said. He also questioned the involvement of the President and National Security while the ownership dispute remained before the court. “Is that law? Is that what is done in the country? Unless the court gives the order,” he said. He made the revelations to Citinews. The Polo Beach Club was demolished on Friday, October 2, during a security-backed clearance operation at the La Beach area. The exercise involved personnel from the Ghana Armed Forces’ 48 Engineer Regiment and the Ghana Police Service and affected several structures, including the Polo Beach Club and La Pleasure Beach. Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations, Stan Dogbe, has said the operation was not part of the government’s flood-mitigation exercise. He said the action was carried out under National Security supervision following a request from the Labadi Beach Hotel over structures and commercial activities along its beachfront. The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), whose investment portfolio includes the Labadi Beach Hotel and La Palm Royal Beach Hotel, also said it had requested National Security intervention over what it described as persistent unlawful occupation, encroachment and unauthorised activities on the beachfront. SSNIT cited concerns including hotel security, unauthorised access, sanitation, environmental damage and the potential impact on its investments. It said the beaches would be cleaned and restored and would remain open to the public. Mr Blay’s allegation that President Mahama personally ordered the demolition has not been independently established in the public accounts of the operation. The demolition has also attracted criticism from the Member of Parliament for La Dadekotopon, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, who said she had been assured that structures around the Labadi Beach area would not be affected and questioned the basis for the operation.

items.title: The Strange Power of Coincidence
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Some coincidences feel a little too perfect to be random. You think about someone you haven’t spoken with in years, and they text you that afternoon. You run into an old friend while traveling in a city neither of you lives in. You learn an unfamiliar word then suddenly seem to encounter it everywhere. Moments like these can feel as though the universe is trying to tell you something. But in a 2016 Atlantic article, Julie Beck explored a less mystical explanation: Coincidences may reveal more about the way our minds work than they do about some hidden order of the world. Statistically, unlikely things happen all the time. Our lives contain so many people, places, conversations, and decisions that there are countless opportunities for strange overlaps to occur. Perhaps what makes a coincidence remarkable, then, is not that it happened but that we noticed it. As a statistician told Beck, a surprising connection might exist without our ever discovering it. In that sense, the special part of a coincidence, in many cases, is our attention to it. Our brains are built to look for these kinds of instances, but knowing this doesn’t necessarily make coincidences less delightful. Maybe we don’t need to decide whether a strange encounter was fate or mere chance. A coincidence can simply remind us how many connections are possible in a life, and how much depends on what we notice. On Coincidences Coincidences and the Meaning of Life By Julie Beck The surprising chances of our lives can seem like they’re hinting at hidden truths, but they’re really revealing the human mind at work. ( From 2016 ) Read the article. What Were My Dreams Trying to Tell Me? By Ayad Akhtar To make sense of my deepest experiences, I needed a new way of talking about the soul. Read the article. The Meaning of Life Is Surprisingly Simple By Arthur C. Brooks You can make your quest for meaning manageable by breaking it down into three bite-size dimensions. ( From 2021 ) Read the article. Still Curious? The missing ingredient of modern life : Ian Bogost on why we need wonder Three paths toward the meaning of life : “Who in the world am I?” asks Alice in Wonderland. It turns out that business school has a useful theory to help you answer that, Arthur C. Brooks wrote in 2023. Other Diversions Taylor Swift’s audience is growing up. Her music is devolving. Why Americans stopped throwing dinner parties Manipulator vs. manipulator PS Courtesy of Hal Y. My colleague Isabel Fattal recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “On Mother’s Day 2021, while on my daily walk, I came across this peafowl, which displayed its feathers. I took this image with my phone and texted it to the moms in my life,” Hal Y., from Palos Verdes Estates, California, wrote. We’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Rafaela

items.title: The Mainstreaming of Anti-Indian Bigotry
items.description: C hristopher Rufo, the conservative activist best known for his opposition to critical race theory, has portrayed his career as one devoted to upholding meritocracy. “The principle, first promised by the Declaration and supported today by a large majority of Americans, would mean that the state would treat all Americans equally, regardless of ancestry, and leave as much discretion as possible to individuals to determine their own futures, without the government imposing or requiring racial favoritism of any kind,” Rufo wrote two years ago in City Journal , a magazine published by the Manhattan Institute, where he is a senior fellow. “Rather than pit ourselves against one another, we should aspire to a higher standard that subordinates racial faction to a broader national identity.” He has urged Republicans to grasp the allure of this ideal, writing last year in The Free Press : “The right now has the winning argument. Americans support a ‘color-blind society’ over a ‘race-conscious society’ by a margin of more than three to one.” And he has depicted opposition to a color-blind meritocracy as a nefarious, left-wing tendency. Rufo’s “briefing book” on critical race theory notes : “Critical race theorists oppose meritocracy, especially standardized testing and competitive admissions in the education system. They claim that meritocracy is a mechanism to uphold racist structures and is derived from ‘racism, nativism, and eugenics.’” Recently, however, Rufo has backed away from his previously forthright defense of meritocracy, and by all available evidence, he has done so because the principle turns out to contain a fatal flaw: Many of the Americans who benefit from meritocracy have brown skin. More to the point, a lot of Republicans resent those brown-skinned Americans. Given the right’s commitment to anti-intellectualism and populist resentment, and President Trump’s open embrace of job promotions based on loyalty or appearance (“central casting”) rather than qualifications, Rufo’s turn against race-blind merit might have been inevitable. Or perhaps his abandonment of the merit principle reveals a great deal about the motives that have driven him all along. The sequence that set in motion Rufo’s conversion began with a social-media post by Bo French, a right-wing activist, the current Republican nominee for Texas railroad commissioner, and a longtime hater of many minority groups, especially Muslims. On September 13, French complained on X about the presence of South Asian students in the crowd at a University of Texas football game. “I heard UT graduation this year looked like this,” French wrote above a picture of the students celebrating. “I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.” [ Jonathan Chait: Bush understood something Trump doesn’t ] Anti-Indian sentiment had been bubbling up on social media for some time. When FBI Director Kash Patel wrote “Happy Diwali” on X last year, his replies were flooded with “ bigoted memes and rhetoric ,” CNN reported. Vivek Ramaswamy, now the Republican nominee for governor in Ohio, wrote in a New York Times op-ed this past December that his feeds are “ littered with hundreds of slurs .” A few days before French’s post, the Department of Homeland Security published an image of Optimus Prime confronting a brown-skinned man along with the words “Self-deport or find out” and “America for Americans. Get off our roads. You don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh.” The DHS post was deleted the next day . But the naked expression of anti-Indian bigotry by a candidate for statewide office signified that it was threatening to enter mainstream Republican politics, a prospect that immediately divided the party. The schism tracked roughly along the same lines as the ones drawn during the initial response to Trump more than a decade ago. The post was met with angry pushback from National Review as well as Texas Senator John Cornyn and Republican strategist Karl Rove—the sorts of Republicans who have tolerated Trump but harbor a not-so-secret desire for the party to return to its pre-MAGA identity. The MAGA right had an altogether more positive response to French’s outburst. Organs such as The Charlie Kirk Show , The Federalist , and the Daily Caller defended it. “Viewers noticed that the Longhorn student section on their TV screens was made up mostly of Indian students. If you are a native Texan, this might have been infuriating, but the demographic makeup wasn’t shocking,” explained the Caller , taking for granted that its audience would find the presence of large numbers of South Asian students at UT Austin outrageous and a cause for anger on its face. The Trump administration weighed in, somewhat more elliptically, on French’s side. The day after French’s post, Trump posted an attack on Rove, who had said he would vote for French’s Democratic opponent in the November election. “Karl Rove is so bad for the Republican Party, and completely wrong so often,” the president wrote on Truth Social . The U.S. Department of Education posted several days later on X , “MAKE COLLEGE FOOTBALL GREAT AGAIN,” above an image of a mostly white crowd in the Texas stadium. Trump’s intervention defined the correct position for the party faithful, as it generally does for any internecine Republican conflict. The attempt by Rove and other traditional Republicans to decree that anti-Indian bigotry was unwelcome inside their party had failed. Instead, Trump had announced that the people condemning racism against South Asians were the ones who did not belong in his coalition. The task for the conservative-movement loyalists who wanted to remain was to rationalize this prejudice. Rufo, a conservative activist-intellectual who had built his reputation by opposing the practice of dividing people by race, was perfectly positioned to finesse this evolutionary step in party dogma. R ufo recorded a podcast this week with Jonathan Keeperman, a right-wing publisher, for an episode they titled “The Indian Question.” One useful historical rule of thumb is that if your social identity is being made the name of a “question,” you are probably not going to like the answer. Rufo conceded that French’s “rhetoric was bad; it’s very crude.” But the crucial question to keep in mind, he told Keeperman, was, “Is the underlying frustration coming from a legitimate place or can it all be dismissed?” They agreed that French’s frustration was legitimate. Rufo later elaborated on his reasoning by saying: “If you live in a suburb of Dallas, suddenly it’s a third or higher percentage new immigrants from India. It causes some disorientation and dislocation, which is legitimate, right?” Resentment of these immigrant communities is understandable, the two men explained, not in spite of the fact that so many South Asians have been successful academically and economically, but because of it. Indian culture, they maintained, places too much value on studying and academic excellence, and these values are a threat to American culture. Indian Americans, Rufo argued, are “going to grind on spelling-bee words like unlimited hours,” whereas American culture says, “You’re not supposed to study for the spelling bee.” Robinson agreed: “What actually makes America so dynamic—it’s not the kid who studies all night for the spelling-bee test. It’s the kid who is the fullback on the high-school football team, who puts his head down and is willing to run through a freaking wall on behalf of his teammates and then spends the night drinking beers at the kegger and wakes up in the morning and gets a 1500 on his SATs, okay?” [ Read: Are you a ‘heritage American’? ] Had a leftist suggested that American culture is defined by alcoholism and disdain for ambition, Rufo would surely decry the remark as a slander. But Keeperman and Rufo seemed to talk themselves into this bizarre version of American exceptionalism. Rufo even began embracing concepts he had once defined as the hallmarks of his left-wing enemies. At one point, Rufo argued that “the right”—he was specifically describing conservatives who oppose anti-Indian racism—has fallen for a pernicious myth. “The right always says”—here he adopted a mocking tone—“ Oh, meritocracy, meritocracy, meritocracy . You morons. Meritocracy, the origin of the term meritocracy, it’s pejorative. It’s satirical. It’s not good. You actually don’t want meritocracy, because it perverts these unspoken cultural assumptions in ways that aren’t always visible, aren’t always, say, rationally defensible or problematic, but they strike at an essential component of the national character.” The man who once depicted meritocracy as the very foundation of the republic now presents it as a sinister threat to American culture. In his Times op-ed, Ramaswamy argued that anti-Indian bigots “have no place in the conservative movement, period.” That debate now appears to be a settled one.

items.title: Le CRLDHT dénonce «l’inhumanité, étendard des prisons en Tunisie»
items.description: «Lorsque des détenus politiques, des journalistes, des avocats et des militants n’ont plus d’autre moyen pour être entendus que de mettre leur santé en jeu» (en observant une grève de la faim), «c’est que la prison est devenue un lieu de négation organisée de la dignité humaine», explique le Centre pour le respect des libertés et des droits de l’homme en Tunisie (CRLDHT), une ONG tunisienne basée en France, dans un communiqué publié ce samedi 3 octobre 2026. Tout en rappelant la longue liste de détenus politiques dans les prisons tunisiennes observant actuellement ou ayant observé récemment la grève de la faim pour dénoncer leurs conditions d’incarcération, cette forme extrême de protestation étant devenue «le dernier recours de celles et ceux à qui l’on a retiré tous les autres moyens de se faire entendre» , le CRDHT «exige le rétablissement immédiat des visites en directe entre les détenus et leurs familles, et la fin de toute restriction arbitraire de ce droit fondamental ; l’accès effectif de tous les détenus à une information pluraliste, à la presse, aux radios, aux chaînes d’information et aux médias indépendants ; un suivi médical régulier, sérieux et indépendant pour tous les grévistes de la faim, ainsi qu’une information complète des familles et des avocats sur leur état de santé ; le respect absolu du droit des détenus à communiquer librement et confidentiellement avec leurs avocats et à disposer des moyens nécessaires à leur défense ; la fin de l’isolement abusif, des mesures punitives, des privations administratives et de toutes les pratiques destinées à épuiser, humilier ou briser les détenus ; l’accès sans entrave aux mécanismes indépendants de contrôle, notamment le Mécanisme national de prévention de la torture, des établissements pénitentiaires et des détenus dont l’état de santé est préoccupant ; la cessation des campagnes de haine, de diffamation et de diabolisation visant les détenus politiques, leurs familles, leurs avocats et les personnes qui les soutiennent ; la libération immédiate et inconditionnelle de toutes les personnes emprisonnées pour leurs opinions, leur droit à l’expression , leur activité politique pacifique, leur travail journalistique, leur défense des droits humains ou leur solidarité civique.» Le CRLDHT appelle, également, les autorités tunisiennes à «cesser de traiter la prison comme un instrument de vengeance politique» , à «protéger la vie et la dignité des détenus n’est ni une faveur, ni une concession» mais «une obligation légale, constitutionnelle et conforme aux droits humains.» Parmi ces détenus politiques ou d’opinion observant actuellement une grève de la faim, le CRLDHT cite Ahmed Néjib Chebbi (83 ans), président du Front de salut national, et Sahbi Atig (67 ans), dirigeant du mouvement Ennahdha. Ils prolongent les nombreuses grèves de la faim déjà observées en prison par Jawher Ben Mbarek, dirigeant du collectif Citoyens contre le coup d’état, les journalistes Zied El Heni et Mourad Zeghidi, mais aussi Rached Ghannouchi (84 ans), président du mouvement Ennahdha, Ayachi Hammami, avocat, Abir Moussi, présidente du Parti destourien libre, Chawki Tabib, ancien bâtonnier, Wael Naouar, animateur de la flottille Soumoud, et ses camarades Ghassen Henchiri, Ghassen Boughdiri et Nabil Chennoufi. I. B. L’article Le CRLDHT dénonce «l’inhumanité, étendard des prisons en Tunisie» est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Nouvelles révélations sur l’affaire Flydubai : le parquet des Émirats qualifie l’incident d’acte terroriste, le copilote déjà écarté des vols
items.description: De nouvelles informations sur le passe de Hamam al-Hammami, le copilote soupconne d'avoir attaque le commandant d'un vol Flydubai reliant Dubaï a Tel Aviv, sont apparues. Selon ABC News, des contenus a caractere extremiste avaient deja ete decouverts en 2024 alors que ce citoyen omanais de 29 ans suivait une formation chez Oman Air. Il aurait ensuite ete ecarte de la formation en vol, tout en restant autorise a travailler dans une fonction administrative. Ces informations apparaissent quelques jours apres l'incident du 30 septembre. Hamam al-Hammami est soupconne d'avoir agresse le commandant de bord avant de tenter de prendre le controle de l'appareil. L'avion avait finalement pu atterrir sans qu'aucun passager ne soit blesse. Le Wall Street Journal rapporte de son cote que les autorites omanaises avaient interdit au pilote de voler en raison d'inquietudes concernant ses opinions radicales. Malgre cette mesure, il a ensuite ete recrute par Flydubai. Les sources disponibles ne precisent pas si ces informations avaient ete transmises a d'autres pays ou compagnies aeriennes. Son parcours professionnel permet egalement de retracer les etapes ayant precede son arrivee chez Flydubai. Selon CNN, un profil LinkedIn attribue au pilote mentionnait sept annees chez Oman Air, jusqu'en fevrier 2025, puis un passage chez Royal Air Maroc entre juin 2025 et janvier 2026. Flydubai n'y figurait pas, alors que plusieurs sources indiquent qu'il y travaillait depuis environ huit mois. Des publications sur des comptes attribues au pilote D'autres elements ont ete releves sur des comptes de reseaux sociaux attribues a Hamam al-Hammami. CNN rapporte que deux publications ont ete mises en ligne environ neuf heures apres l'incident du 30 septembre. Rien ne permet toutefois d'affirmer qu'il les a publiees lui-meme, puisqu'elles auraient pu etre programmees a l'avance. L'une d'elles montrait notamment des images de cockpits de Boeing 737 MAX ainsi que des appareils des compagnies israeliennes El Al et Arkia. La sequence se terminait par des photographies d'Ayman al-Zawahiri, ancien chef d'Al-Qaïda, et de Humam Khalil al-Balawi, auteur d'un attentat en 2009 ayant notamment tue sept employes et sous-traitants de la CIA. Al Arabiya affirme egalement que Hamam al-Hammami aurait sejourne en Syrie et avance qu'il aurait pu y etre expose a des idees radicales. Cette information reste cependant attribuee au media. a ce stade, aucune des sources citees n'etablit de lien formel entre le pilote et une organisation terroriste. Les emirats arabes unis qualifient l'incident d'acte terroriste L'enquete a egalement franchi une nouvelle etape aux emirats arabes unis. Le 3 octobre, le procureur general Hamad Saif al-Shamsi a indique que l'incident a bord du vol Flydubai etait desormais qualifie d'acte terroriste. Selon le procureur general, l'enquete a etabli que le copilote prevoyait de commettre un attentat. Il aurait frappe le commandant avec une hache de secours specialement conservee dans le cockpit pour les situations d'urgence, avant de tenter de prendre le controle de l'appareil. Les autorites emiraties poursuivent leurs investigations afin de preciser ses motivations, ses eventuels contacts et les autres elements lies a l'affaire. Hamad Saif al-Shamsi a souligne que l'enquete etait toujours en cours. ABC News rapporte par ailleurs que Hamam al-Hammami coopere avec les enqueteurs et aurait reconnu avoir voulu provoquer le crash de l'appareil en Israel. Cette affirmation reste attribuee au media. Les circonstances dans lesquelles un pilote deja ecarte des vols a Oman a ensuite pu etre recrute par Flydubai restent egalement a eclaircir. Pour l'heure, les elements cites n'etablissent pas l'existence d'un commanditaire ni l'appartenance du suspect a une organisation precise.

items.title: WHO lists top 10 causes of death globally
items.description: The World Health Organisation (WHO) says ischaemic heart disease and stroke were the leading causes of death globally in 2023, accounting for more than 16 million deaths combined. The health agency disclosed this on Friday in its latest report on the top global causes of death. Ischaemic heart disease, caused by narrowed or blocked arteries that reduce blood flow and oxygen to the heart muscle, was responsible for about 9.5 million deaths in 2023, representing 16 percent of all deaths globally. Stroke ranked second, causing about 6.8 million deaths, or 11 percent of global deaths, while chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) was the third leading cause, with about 3.6 million deaths. Lower respiratory infections ranked fourth, accounting for 2.7 million deaths, followed by Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias, which caused about 2.1 million deaths. The WHO said eight of the 10 leading causes of death globally in 2023 were non-communicable diseases (NCDs), which accounted for 74 per cent of all deaths worldwide, compared with 58 per cent in 2000. Other leading causes included diabetes, trachea, bronchus and lung cancers, hypertensive heart disease, kidney diseases and diarrhoeal diseases. According to the WHO, the 10 leading causes of death collectively accounted for 33 million deaths, representing 54 per cent of the 61 million deaths recorded globally in 2023. It said cardiovascular diseases remained the leading cause of death and disease burden worldwide. “There has been substantial progress in reducing the burden of ischaemic heart disease since 2000 in many parts of the world,” the report said. “However, increases in risk at an individual level were recorded in the WHO Western Pacific and South-East Asia Regions, highlighting persistent inequalities in cardiovascular health between populations.” The WHO said global life expectancy recovered to 73.3 years in 2023, close to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019 before the COVID-19 pandemic. TOP 10 Ischaemic heart disease Stroke Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease Lower respiratory infections Alzheimer disease and other dementias Diabetes mellitus Trachea, bronchus, lung cancers Hypertensive heart disease Kidney diseases Diarrhoeal diseases The post WHO lists top 10 causes of death globally appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘We’ve complied with all the rules’ – NPP assures transparency in national elections
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it has put in place measures to ensure transparency and compliance with electoral rules ahead of its national officers’ elections in Kumasi. The party’s Director of Elections, Evans Nimako, said the election organisers had complied with the required rules and standards and had taken steps to give all aspirants access to the relevant delegate registers. Speaking ahead of the party’s National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, Mr Nimako said all aspirants had been provided with both provisional and final delegates’ registers. “We’ve complied with all the rules and standards to make this election transparent.” He added that the accreditation of delegates had also been completed ahead of the exercise. “All aspirants were given provisional and final register and we’ve accredited all delegates.” Mr Nimako said the measures formed part of efforts to ensure that the internal elections were conducted in accordance with the party’s rules and applicable electoral guidelines. The NPP is expected to elect its national officers at the conference, with the Electoral Commission (EC) set to conduct the election under the supervision of the party’s National Officers Elections Committee. The party had earlier said concerns raised by aspirants over the delegates’ register were reviewed during the validation process, with the committee checking disputed names and details against source records submitted by regions and institutions. The elections are scheduled to take place at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, with thousands of accredited delegates expected to participate.

items.title: Équipe de France : Dayot Upamecano quitte le rassemblement après son expulsion contre l’Italie
items.description: Le défenseur central de l'équipe de France Dayot Upamecano a quitté, samedi, le rassemblement des Bleus après son expulsion lors de la rencontre face à l'Italie vendredi soir en Ligue des nations (1-1), a indiqué la Fédération française de football. Le joueur du Bayern Munich sera suspendu pour le match contre les « Diables rouges » lundi prochain au Stade de France, après avoir reçu un deuxième carton jaune à la suite d'une faute commise sur l'attaquant de la Squadra Azzurra Moïse Kean, à la 85e minute. Après le forfait de Kylian Mbappé, rentré à Madrid pour une blessure en Turquie le 25 septembre, le groupe de Zinédine Zidane se retrouve encore réduit à 21 joueurs avant l'ultime match de cette première trêve internationale sous les ordres du nouveau sélectionneur, lundi contre la Belgique à domicile. Les Bleus, qui restent sur deux victoires 1-0 en Turquie puis en Belgique, ont dû partager vendredi les points pour la première fois sous la direction de Zidane. Dans l'autre match de ce groupe, la Belgique s'est largement imposée face à la Turquie (3-0), grâce notamment à un doublé de Kevin De Bruyn. Après trois journées, la France reste ainsi en tête du classement avec un total de 7 points, devant la Belgique (6 pts) et l'Italie (4 pts), alors que la Turquie ferme la marche à l'issue de trois défaites consécutives. The post Équipe de France : Dayot Upamecano quitte le rassemblement après son expulsion contre l’Italie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JEPPC 2026 : Le ministre Sana présente les acquis dans la modernisation de son département
items.description: Le ministre de la Sécurité, le Commissaire divisionnaire de Police Mahamadou Sana, a exposé, le vendredi 2 octobre 2026, les réalisations de son département sur la période 2022-2026, dans le cadre de l'Exposition gouvernementale organisée à l'occasion de la deuxième phase de la 3e édition des Journées nationales d'engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne (JEPPC). Le renforcement des effectifs, la montée en puissance des unités spécialisées, la lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité urbaine, la transformation numérique des services ainsi que l'amélioration de la sécurité routière sont les avancées mises en exergue. Une vue des officiels Face à un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement exigeant, le Ministère de la Sécurité a engagé plusieurs réformes et actions structurantes visant à renforcer les capacités des Forces de sécurité intérieure (FSI), tout en améliorant l'offre sécuritaire au profit des populations. Lors de la présentation des réalisations du département ministériel, plusieurs chiffres et actions ont été mis en avant par le ministre Mahamadou Sana pour illustrer les efforts consentis au cours de la période 2022-2026. Selon les données qu'il a présentées, d'importants recrutements ont été effectués au sein des FSI. Le ministre a fait état de 2 000 recrutements multipliés par trois au niveau des Eaux et Forêts et de 2 000 recrutements multipliés par cinq au niveau de la Police nationale. « Cette augmentation des effectifs a contribué à améliorer le ratio agent/population, passé de 1 agent pour 648 habitants en 2021 à 1 pour 537 en juin 2026 », a-t-il déclaré. Le nombre d'unités spécialisées est également passé de 16 en 2022 à 58 en 2026, avec notamment la montée en puissance de la BAC, de la CRS, des GUMI, du GSIPN, de l'UMI et de l'UCEF. À cela s'ajoute l'acquisition de plus de 10 000 motos et 155 véhicules adaptés aux opérations. La lutte contre le terrorisme au cœur des priorités Sur le front de la lutte contre le terrorisme, le Commissaire divisionnaire de Police, Mahamadou Sana a mis en avant une progression du taux de maîtrise du territoire national, passé de 37,88 % à 74,53 %. Il a également relevé l'opérationnalisation des centres des opérations de la Police nationale, de la Gendarmerie nationale ainsi que du Centre de Coordination des Opérations du ministère de la Sécurité, une stru (CCO/MSECU). Le renforcement de la formation, de l'équipement et de l'aguerrissement des unités combattantes, ainsi que l'adaptation des stratégies opérationnelles, ont également été cités parmi les actions menées. Dans le domaine de la lutte contre la criminalité urbaine, le ministre Sana a notamment cité le déploiement des opérations WIBGA 1, 2 et 3, ainsi que l’opération Koglégo. « Le concept S24/7, qui met en relation la vidéoprotection, la Police secours et la BAC est un dispositif destiné à renforcer la réponse opérationnelle », a-t-il ajouté. Le commissaire Sana a fait par ailleurs état d'une réduction du taux moyen de criminalité urbaine, ainsi que d'une intensification des contrôles, des patrouilles et des actions de renseignement. La sécurité investit dans le numérique La modernisation numérique constitue également l'un des axes mis en avant. Le ministère a notamment créé la Brigade numérique de veille, d'assistance et d'alerte (BNVAA) et lancé la plateforme Alerte BCLCC. Une vue des participants Des antennes régionales de la Brigade centrale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (BCLCC) et de la Brigade spéciale des investigations antiterroristes et de lutte contre la criminalité organisée (BSIAT) ont également été ouvertes. La dématérialisation de certains outils de travail, notamment la main courante et le SYGESS, figure aussi parmi les acquis présentés Un studio multimédia a par ailleurs été créé, notamment pour contribuer à la détection et à la démonstration des fake news. Dans le domaine de la sécurité routière, Mahamadou Sana a mis en avant le renforcement des capacités de l'ONASER, l'application du Règlement n°14 relatif aux charges à l'essieu, ainsi que la généralisation de la vidéoverbalisation et de la e-contravention. La création de la BRICIR figure également parmi les mesures présentées à ce niveau. D'après les données communiquées, le taux de port du casque est passé de 8,7 % à plus de 95 %, tandis qu'une baisse de la prévalence des accidents de la circulation est annoncée. Le ministère a également mis en lumière le développement d'une approche davantage tournée vers les populations dont la Brigade Laabal et la plateforme Alerte Laabal. La Police Yaka, les commissariats mobiles et la police communautaire sont présentés comme des mécanismes visant à rapprocher davantage les services de sécurité des citoyens. Plus de 4 400 personnes auraient par ailleurs été encadrées dans le cadre des travaux d'intérêt général. Sur le volet environnemental, le bilan fait état de plus 31 millions de plants mis en terre, ainsi que la création de la Brigade Yiri Dêmê et la réhabilitation du parc Bangr-Wéogo. Mahamadou Sanaa indiqué également avoir procédé à une répartition des zones de compétence entre la Police nationale et la Gendarmerie nationale, avec pour objectif de rationaliser les moyens et d'améliorer le maillage sécuritaire. La lutte contre la corruption et les rackets, la réduction des postes de contrôle ainsi que l'organisation d’exercices conjoints de simulation d'attaques complexes à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso ont également été citées. En termes de perspectives, le ministère entend poursuivre toujours selon Mahamadou Sana la reconquête et la sécurisation du territoire, accélérer la transformation numérique des services de sécurité et développer davantage une approche préventive. Le renforcement du civisme, du patriotisme et de la participation citoyenne figure également parmi les perspectives annoncées. Jean-François SOMÉ Minute.bf

items.description: CAIRO/GAZA, Oct 3 (Reuters) - An Israeli airstrike killed at least five Palestinians, including four women, in an apartment building in Gaza City early on Saturday, health and civil defense service officials said. Among the dead were a Christian mother and her daughter, medics said. There was no immediate comment from the Israeli military. The strike destroyed the apartment building and started a fire.

items.title: Man arrested in Fairford air base investigation released on bail
items.description: LONDON, Oct 3 (Reuters) - British counter-terrorism police investigating a suspected plot involving an air base used by the US said on Saturday they had released on bail a dual UK-Iranian national who had been arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. The 25-year-old man was detained on Thursday over the incident last weekend involving the RAF Fairford base in western England from where US bombers have taken part in raids against targets in Iran. items.title: ‘Who is financing all this?’ – Victoria Bright questions networks behind Ghana-linked drug trade
items.description: International corporate lawyer and entrepreneur Victoria Bright says Ghana must move beyond focusing on individual drug seizures and investigate the wider organised crime networks facilitating the trafficking of narcotics through the country. Speaking on Newsfile, she said the repeated seizures of Ghana-linked drug consignments point to a broader problem that requires scrutiny of the systems and institutions being exploited by traffickers. “We have to go beyond these individual drug seizures and examine the wider questions of organised crime, these allegations of political influence, institutional accountability, and our vulnerability as a transit point for international drug traffickers.” She said the frequency and scale of recent seizures are particularly concerning because consignments linked to Ghana have been intercepted through different channels, including commercial containers, road transport and passenger aviation. According to Ms Bright, some of the largest consignments linked to Ghana have not been detected locally but were intercepted after reaching Europe and other destinations. She therefore questioned how trafficking networks are able to consistently move drugs through Ghana’s ports and airports and whether they have gained access to or influence within state institutions. “How extensive really are these networks, and how are they consistently getting through our ports and our airports? Who is financing all this, and who is ultimately benefiting from these trades?” She argued that the issue should be treated as a broader national security and institutional accountability concern rather than simply a matter of arresting individuals whenever a drug shipment is intercepted. “We have to treat this issue now as a serious national security and institutional integrity question rather than just a series of big drug busts.”

items.title: «Le réel nous rattrape» : le taux d’emprunt de la France a frôlé les 5%, une première depuis 2002
items.description: La France tiendra-t-elle jusqu'aux prochaines elections presidentielles ? Alors que le gouvernement Lecornu fait face a une enieme crise interne, avec la « fronde » lyceenne , et qu'il vient de presenter un budget presentant de nouvelles hausses des depenses et des prelevements, nombre d'observateurs economiques tirent le signal d'alarme face a la crise financiere qui prend forme. « On est en train de se demander comment vont se passer ces elections apaisees, tel qu'on y va – la on y va franchement – cela risque d'etre une crise financiere extremement grave », a alerte le 1er octobre sur France TV l'economiste Philippe Dessertine, qui ne croit « absolument pas » que l'objectif de 5 % de deficit du PLF presente par le gouvernement Lecornu sera tenu et qui souligne au passage que ce budget de « redressement » contient 42 milliards d'augmentation de depenses. Ce jour-la, le taux d'emprunt de la France sur le marche obligataire secondaire a atteint les 4,96 %, un record depuis juillet 2002, avant de revenir aux alentours de 4,92 % le 2 octobre, sur fond de leger reflux des cours de l'or noir. Dorenavant, le coût de la dette francaise depasse les plus hauts qu'il avait atteint durant la crise financiere de 2007-2008. Le spread France-Allemagne flambe Soulignons que dans le cadre du marche obligataire, dont le fonctionnement peut paraître au premier abord contre-intuitif, une hausse du rendement des obligations traduit une vente de ces dernieres par leurs detenteurs : le taux monte alors afin de tenter les acheteurs. Temoignage de cette defiance vis-a-vis de la France, alors que le phenomene affecte l'Europe et les etats-Unis, le spread, a savoir l'ecart entre le taux d'emprunt de la France et celui de l'Allemagne – qui fait figure de reference sur le Vieux continent – a depasse les 150 points de base le 2 octobre, une premiere depuis fin 2011. « Le reel nous rattrape », avait lance sur X Sebastien Lecornu le 30 septembre, a la veille de la presentation du projet de budget de son gouvernement. Un budget de « redressement », avait-il promis. Un budget qui devrait notamment se traduire par une hausse des prelevements obligatoires, et ce, alors meme que la France figure sur le podium des pays ou l'on taxe le plus.

items.title: Pomme de terre : le gouvernement plafonne les prix à 80-90 DA
items.description: Face à la flambée des prix de la pomme de terre qui dure depuis plusieurs semaines en Algérie, le gouvernement a pris une mesure importante pour réguler le marché. Les prix de ce produit de large consommation ont dépassé les 100 dinars le kilogramme, atteignant 140 dinars dans certains marchés d’Alger, contre 50-70 dinars en temps normal. Le prix de la pomme de terre plafonné à 80-90 dinars le kilogramme La question a fait l’objet d’une réunion interministérielle jeudi 1er octobre, à l’issue de laquelle un accord a été conclu avec les représentants de la profession pour plafonner les prix de la vente au consommateur de la pomme de terre à 80-90 dinars maximum. La décision a été notifiée le jour même par le ministère du Commerce intérieur et de la Régulation du marché national aux directeurs du commerce des wilayas. “ Un accord a été conclu avec les représentants de diverses filières professionnelles agricoles, les représentants des petites, moyennes et grandes exploitations agricoles, ainsi que les représentants des exploitants de chambres froides, afin de plafonner le prix de vente de la pomme de terre destinée aux consommateurs comme suit : le prix de vente du producteur se situe entre 60 et 70 dinars algériens ; le prix de vente au détail pour le consommateur se situe entre 80 et 90 dinars algériens ”, lit-on dans la note du ministère. Les services de contrôle instruits de veiller au strict respect des prix Les directeurs du commerce des wilayas sont instruits d’ordonner aux services de contrôle de veiller au strict respect des prix de vente arrêtés à tous les stades de la commercialisation, et de fournir à l’administration centrale des rapports quotidiens sur la mise en œuvre de cette instruction. En avril 2025, le gouvernement avait plafonné les prix de cinq produits, la banane, la pomme, la pomme de terre, la viande d'agneau et la tasse de café dans les cafés. Pour certains de ces produits, la mesure n’a pas été suivie d'effet, comme c'est le cas de la banane, plafonnée à 400 dinars le kilogramme mais qui a fini par dépasser les 2000 dinars. items.title: If we don’t know Baffour Awuah’s charge, there’s a fishing expedition going on – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Lawyer and Senior Vice President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has questioned the circumstances surrounding the arrest of lawyer Baffour Awuah, saying that the failure to clearly state the charge against him raises serious procedural concerns. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 3, during a discussion on the Baffour Awuah-EOCO case and related matters, Mr Bentil said authorities should be able to tell an arrested person why they are being detained. “My first question is, what has he been charged with?” he asked. Mr Bentil said the issue was important because the exercise of state power to arrest an individual must be accompanied by a clear explanation of the reason for the arrest. “You and I know that to arrest somebody, you tell the person what they are being arrested for,” he said. “So there’s a certain procedural problem there, and that is a big issue.” Mr Bentil said his concerns were heightened by the fact that, according to him, Mr Awuah had still not been charged after several days. “If you amass the powers of the state to go after a person in the proper performance of his duties in this manner, and you have not even after three days charged the person, I see a big problem,” he said. He acknowledged that Mr Awuah had been arrested but questioned what offence he was alleged to have committed. “Have they arrested him? Yes,” Mr Bentil said. “But I say that if at this point we don’t know what he’s being charged with, I see a problem there.” It was this uncertainty that led him to question whether the investigation was being pursued without a clearly established offence. “I think there’s a fishing expedition going on,” he said. Mr Bentil also questioned why the matter had escalated to the level of a criminal investigation and arrest, arguing that, based on his understanding, the dispute appeared to be a civil matter involving a lawyer and a client. “Because as far as I can see, this is a civil matter between a lawyer and a client, and I don’t know why it rises to the point,” he said. He also questioned the priorities of state investigative agencies, saying there were other matters in the country that, in his view, demanded more urgent scrutiny. “And I’m saying there are so many other things going on today in this country which absolutely warrant far more intense investigation which are left undone,” he said. Despite his concerns about the arrest and the absence of a clearly stated charge, Mr Bentil said the matter should be allowed to proceed through Ghana’s legal and institutional processes. He said the country’s democratic system had established institutions with defined responsibilities and that those institutions should operate within the law. “So look, we will all wait for the process,” he said. “We set up this democracy with institutions to perform their duties according to law. And at the end of the day, we will be able to assess what has been done,” he said.

items.title: INEC warns Nigerians against fake voter registration website
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned Nigerians against a fake website claiming that the online voter registration exercise is currently ongoing. The commission, in a public notice on Saturday, said the website, pvc-inecnigeria-org.blogspot.com, falsely announced a nationwide registration window from September 28 to October 27, 2026. INEC said the platform has no affiliation with the commission and urged Nigerians not to click on the link or provide personal information on the website. “Members of the public are strongly advised not to click on the link or submit any personal information on the website, as doing so may expose them to the risk of having their sensitive personal data harvested or misused,” the notice posted on X reads. “The Commission further wishes to clarify that the voter registration exercise closed on 26th July 2026. Any information suggesting that a new nationwide online voter registration exercise is currently ongoing through the above mentioned website is false. “INEC urges the public to remain vigilant and to verify all electoral information through the Commission’s official communication channels.” The website claims to offer a “Final Phase of Nationwide Online Voter Card Registration”, including services to update voter registration details, transfer registration to another polling unit, and replace damaged or lost permanent voter cards (PVCs), adding that voter registration and PVC delivery are free. INEC urged Nigerians to remain vigilant and verify electoral information through the commission’s official communication channels. The post INEC warns Nigerians against fake voter registration website appeared first on Vanguard News .
