items.title: Le drame de Yakine ou le non confisqué
items.description: À Tunis, une adolescente, Yakine, est devenue le centre d’une enquête pour agression sexuelle présumée. Autour d’elle, versions contradictoires, arrestations, recherches et rumeurs. Mais derrière le fait divers, une question plus silencieuse apparaît : qu’apprenons-nous réellement à nos enfants lorsqu’il s’agit de leur corps, de leurs limites et du refus de l’autre ? Manel Albouchi * Dans une époque saturée d’images et de jugements instantanés, la retenue est déjà une responsabilité. Depuis quelques jours, l’affaire de Yakine, une jeune fille qui a subi des violences ayant nécessité son hospitalisation, suscite une vive émotion en Tunisie. Une société entière s'est mise à regarder. Les spéculations se sont multipliées, des récits se sont construits sur des informations fragmentaires, et plusieurs se sont improvisés profilers en dressant déjà le profil psychologique de personnes dont la responsabilité n’est pas établie par la justice. Mais, l’enquête sur cette affaire délicate se poursuit et nous ne savons pas encore tout. Entre indignation et intrusion Regarder sans posséder. C’est ici qu’il faut tracer une frontière nette entre deux mouvements collectifs. D’un côté, l’opposition saine : poser des balises, refuser la banalisation de la violence, exiger la vérité et protéger les droits fondamentaux. De l’autre, l’intrusion destructrice : partager photos, prénoms, vidéos et rumeurs. La victime réelle devient alors un personnage collectif, et son intimité, une conversation nationale. ​Cette seconde pente dit quelque chose de notre lien social. Le lynchage médiatique ou virtuel est une pathologie contemporaine : une foule jetée en pâture à l’émotion brute, nourrie par le sensationnalisme, où la justice et la complexité sont étouffées par le vacarme de l’opinion. ​Une mineure victime de violences n’est pas un symbole ou le support de nos colères. Les autorités ont appelé à préserver sa vie privée. Même lorsque nous voulons nous indigner, nous devons respecter ses limites et ne pas transformer son drame en spectacle. Avant la théorie, il y a un corps. Un corps qui peut être blessé, contraint, et dont le propriétaire devrait rester celui qui l’habite. Le premier non de l’enfant Toute l’éducation au consentement commence bien avant l’adolescence, dans les gestes ordinaires : entre «Donne un bisou à…» ; et «Tu veux faire un bisou ?» ; «Non.» «D’accord.» Ces deux scènes minuscules enseignent une double évidence : mon corps m’appartient ; le corps de l’autre lui appartient. Le premier «non» de l’enfant est rarement confortable ; l’adulte y voit parfois de l’insolence. Pourtant, respecter le refus de l’enfant ne signifie pas abolir l’autorité. La psychologie du développement distingue avec précision le soutien à l’autonomie du contrôle psychologique. Une vaste méta-analyse portant sur 238 études (Bradshaw et al., American Psychologist, 2025) confirme sur plus de 126 000 participants l’association profonde entre le soutien parental à l’autonomie et l’épanouissement des enfants, tandis que le contrôle psychologique se trouve invariablement lié aux indicateurs de mal-être, et ce, à travers toutes les cultures. Une autorité juste ( «Je ne peux pas te laisser faire cela, car c’est dangereux» ) pose les limites nécessaires à la sécurité. Le contrôle psychologique ( «Tu n’as pas le droit de vouloir autre chose que moi» ) étouffe le sujet. Le deuxième non Il existe un apprentissage symétrique, tout aussi difficile : apprendre à recevoir le non de l’autre. «Je ne veux pas.» Cette phrase peut produire de la déception, de la frustration, parfois de la colère. Mais elle ne constitue pas nécessairement une injustice. L’autre peut ne pas vouloir, ne pas aimer ce que j’aime, refuser mon invitation, interrompre une relation ou ne pas répondre à mon désir. Et je peux souffrir de ce refus sans avoir pour autant un droit sur celui qui me refuse. Le désir ne crée pas un droit. La frustration ne crée pas une dette chez l’autre. Le refus de l’autre n’est pas automatiquement une attaque contre moi. Mon désir n’est pas ton désir. Ma colère n’est pas ton obligation. Mon corps n’est pas ton territoire, ton corps n’est pas le mien. Je peux t’aimer et accepter ton refus. Tu peux m’aimer et refuser quelque chose. Cette séparation n’est pas une rupture du lien : elle en est la condition. Car si l’autre doit vouloir ce que je veux pour rester proche de moi, il n’est jamais véritablement autre : il devient une extension de mon désir. Après le drame | Quand une société demande à l’école de réparer ses propres fractures La confiscation du non ​Lorsqu’un enfant apprend de manière répétée à renoncer à ses propres limites (parce que sa colère est systématiquement invalidée ou son refus qualifié d’insolence), il risque d’intégrer que la volonté du plus fort l’emporte toujours. ​Bien entendu, cela ne désigne en rien une fatalité et ne jette le discrédit ni sur les familles ni sur les victimes. Sur le plan clinique, ces contextes de confiscation précoce constituent toutefois un terrain propice où certaines difficultés risquent de se déployer au fil des âges. A l’adolescence : la vulnérabilité face aux emprises. Faute d’avoir pu expérimenter la valeur de son «non» dans un cadre sécurisant, le jeune adulte en devenir peut se retrouver plus désarmé face aux pressions extérieures, s'exposant plus facilement à des influences ou à des dynamiques d’emprise. ​En couple : les tourments de la dépendance affective. Plus tard, l’adulte risque de s’oublier dans ses relations amoureuses par peur panique du rejet. Par un mouvement symétrique, l’absence d’exposition au «non» de l’autre rend parfois la frustration intolérable, faisant basculer la relation entre angoisse fusionnelle et besoin de contrôle. Au travail : l’épuisement et le faux-self. Cette incapacité à poser des limites peut mener à une suradaptation chronique. L’adulte endosse alors un « faux-self », ce masque social et protecteur façonné pour plaire et répondre aux attentes de la performance, au risque de s’épuiser, voire de glisser vers le burn-out par peur de l'exclusion. ​Dans la relation parentale : l’enfant comme extension. C’est parfois là que la boucle se boucle. Un parent lui-même carencé dans son histoire personnelle peut tisser un lien fusionnel où l’enfant est inconsciemment perçu comme une extension de soi. Le moindre «non» de l’enfant est alors vécu non comme une saine étape d'individuation, mais comme une menace existentielle. ​Du foyer à la société ​ Ce qui se tisse dans l’intimité du foyer résonne inévitablement au-delà de ses murs. Une éducation qui confisque la nuance et le refus cultive insensiblement un terreau de docilité, où l’obéissance finit par l’emporter sur l’esprit critique. Le pli pris face à l’injonction absolue ( «parce que je l’ai dit» ) prépare le terrain à d’autres formes de soumission face au dogme ou à l’arbitraire. ​De même, à plus grande échelle, les structures pyramidales ou les climats sous tension partagent parfois cette même allergie à la contradiction : lorsque le désaccord est reçu non comme un dialogue, mais comme une insubordination, c'est toute la vitalité démocratique qui s’étiole. L’intolérance au «non» (qu’elle s’exerce à l’échelle d’une maison ou dans les rouages du pouvoir obéit toujours à la même grammaire de l’emprise. ​Qu’apprenons-nous à nos enfants lorsqu’ils disent non ? ​L’enjeu éducatif n’est ni de supprimer l’autorité ni de fabriquer des enfants qui disent non à tout, mais de construire une relation où l’enfant comprend que son non compte, que celui de l’autre compte aussi, et qu’il peut être frustré sans être victime d’une injustice. ​C’est là que l’autonomie rencontre l’empathie. Alors, la véritable question que nous laisse l’affaire de Yakine n’est pas seulement «comment en sommes-nous arrivés là ?» , mais plus profondément : qu’apprenons-nous à nos enfants lorsqu’ils disent non ? ​Car un enfant à qui l’on apprend que son non a une valeur comprend aussi que celui de l’autre compte. Et la culture du consentement commence exactement là : dans la façon dont un adulte, face à un enfant qui refuse, sait répondre simplement : «D’accord. J’ai entendu.» * Psychothérapeute. L’article Le drame de Yakine ou le non confisqué est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

Follow the evidence, not assumptions, in Baffour Awuah case – Victoria Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer Victoria Bright has urged the public to allow the evidence to guide discussions surrounding the case involving Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah and the Economic and Organised Crime Office’s (EOCO) investigation into the SIC Life Savings and Loans transaction. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 3, Ms Bright said the controversy should not be reduced to a simple choice between justice and political power play. She said there were two separate questions that needed to be considered: whether EOCO had a legitimate basis to investigate the underlying transaction, and whether the office had exercised its investigative powers lawfully, proportionately and fairly. “For me, we need to resist the temptation to reduce this matter to a simple choice between justice and power play,” she said. “There are two separate questions, and it’s important that we don’t conflate the two questions.” Ms Bright said information already available in the public domain raised questions about the transaction that, in her view, warranted investigation. She identified the settlement, the authorisation for the movement of funds and what she described as apparent anomalies in the documentation as areas requiring scrutiny. “From what we have seen in the public domain, I believe that there are questions that do warrant investigation about the settlement, questions about the settlement, who authorised the movement of funds and some apparent anomalies in the documentation,” she said. However, she said that establishing a basis for an investigation was separate from examining how EOCO exercised its powers during that investigation. “And we know they have considerable powers,” she said, adding that the question was “whether those powers are being exercised lawfully, proportionately, and fairly in pursuing their investigation.” According to Ms Bright, the two issues must be examined independently because the legitimacy of an investigation does not automatically settle questions about the conduct of the investigation. “It’s possible for an investigation to be legitimate while aspects of the manner in which it is conducted raise legitimate rule of law concerns,” she said. She therefore urged caution against drawing conclusions before all the relevant evidence had been properly examined. “So for me, it’s important that we follow the evidence rather than presume either guilt or political prosecution,” Ms Bright said. A major issue she believes requires closer examination is the GH¢5 million settlement at the centre of the controversy. Ms Bright said the key questions should include whether the amount represented a commercially defensible compromise of a difficult judgment debt and, importantly, whether the decision to accept the settlement had been properly authorised. “One of the questions we should be asking ourselves is whether the 5 million cedis is a commercially defensible compromise of a difficult judgment debt,” she said. “And whether that compromise, if so, whether that compromise was properly authorised.” For her, establishing who had the authority to settle on behalf of SIC is particularly important. “Who authorised the settlement on behalf of SIC?” she asked. Ms Bright noted that questions had been raised about the authority of the SIC official allegedly involved in the transaction. However, she said the issue should ultimately be capable of being resolved through documents. “I know that Yuriko is questioning the authority of the lady, the SIC official who was involved in all of this, or allegedly involved in all of this,” she said. “But for me, that should be capable of documentary resolution.” Ms Bright said investigators and the public should be looking for specific documents that could establish how the settlement decision was reached. Among the questions she raised was whether a board resolution existed and whether authority had been formally delegated. “Was there a board resolution? Was authority delegated?” she asked. She also questioned what instructions had been given to the lawyers representing SIC and what the engagement agreement between the company and its lawyers provided. “What instructions were given to the lawyers? Where is the lawyer’s engagement contract with SIC? What does it say?” she said. Another important question, she said, was who approved the GH¢5 million figure and what legal advice had been received about continuing enforcement of the judgment debt. “Who actually approved the figure of 5 million cedis? And what advice was received about continuing enforcement?” she asked. Ms Bright said the answers could establish whether the settlement was the result of a properly authorised commercial decision or whether someone acted without the necessary authority. “If properly authorised management made a commercial decision after receiving advice, then that presents one factual picture,” she said. “Conversely, if someone without authority surrendered a substantial judgment debt, then that presents a different matter altogether.” Ms Bright also cautioned against assuming that an unfavourable or unsuccessful commercial decision necessarily amounts to wrongdoing. She noted that businesses make difficult decisions every day, some of which may appear unwise when viewed later. “We need to remember that,” she said. “Because commercial decisions are made every day that subsequently may look unwise,” she added.

items.title: 11 terrorists killed during operations in KP, Balochistan: state media
items.description: Security forces killed 11 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Saturday. State-run Radio Pakistan reported that five Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists had been killed during an IBO in KP’s South Waziristan district. Quoting security sources, the report said that security forces were continuing effective operations against Fitna al-Khawarij in KP under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision. The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. “The security forces targeted and destroyed the hideouts of Fitna al Khawarij during the successful operation, killing five terrorists,” state media said, “A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was also recovered from the killed terrorists.” “The Fitna al Khawarij terrorists are suffering heavy losses in intelligence-based operations, being conducted in KP,” Radio Pakistan quoted the security sources as saying. “Security forces are committed to completely eliminate the menace of terrorism and ensure sustainable peace in the country under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision,” the security sources said. In a separate operation, PTV News reported that security forces killed six terrorists in the Gorander and Mashkel areas of Balochistan during an operation. “Security forces continue effective operations against Fitna al Hindustan under Operation Raddul Fitna 3,” the report said, quoting the security sources. State media, citing security sources, said that the terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan attempted to flee after opening fire on a security checkpost in Mashkel. “Security forces responded promptly and killed the fleeing terrorists,” according to security sources. “Security forces remain determined under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision to completely eliminate the scourge of terrorism from across the country,” the security sources affirmed. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time. The province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in KP’s Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in KP’s Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Monday, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan. Last week, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation . On Sept 17, security forces killed 10 terrorists in separate operations in KP between Sept 15 and 17. Earlier in the month, over 20 terrorists were killed during multiple engagements in KP between Sept 3 and 5.

items.title: Travaux de basculement du nouveau poste de Bel Air : perturbations sur la fourniture d’électricité du 3 du 5 octobre
items.description: Des perturbations sur la fourniture d'électricité pourraient être observées du samedi 3 au lundi 5 octobre 2026, à cause du basculement des ouvrages du poste de Bel Air vers un nouveau poste GIS de dernière génération. C’est ce qu’a indiqué la Senelec dans un communiqué du 2 octobre 2026. Dans le cadre de son programme de modernisation et de renforcement des infrastructures électriques, réalisé avec l'appui du Millennium Challenge Account (MCA), Senelec procédera, du samedi 3 au lundi 5 octobre 2026, au basculement des ouvrages du poste de Bel Air vers un nouveau poste GIS de dernière génération. Ce nouvel équipement stratégique va renforcer, selon la Senelec, la fiabilité et la sécurité du réseau électrique de Dakar et permettra de mieux répondre à la hausse constante de la demande en énergie dans la capitale. A lire aussi : Délestages : Senelec table sur un retour à la normale d’ici la fin de la semaine « Cette opération nécessitera momentanément, une mise hors tension de certains ouvrages et entrainera une réduction provisoire des capacités de production de la centrale de Karpowership. Des perturbations pourraient donc être observées sur la fourniture d'électricité pendant cette période d'intervention, du 3 au 5 octobre 2026, notamment dans les environs de Bel Air », lit-on dans le communiqué de la Senelec. Sur ce, Senelec présente ses excuses pour les éventuels désagréments occasionnés et remercie sa clientèle pour sa compréhension. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Tinubu reforms raise oil output by 80% — Lokpobiri
items.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, has said reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu have increased Nigeria’s crude oil production by more than 80 per cent. Lokpobiri stated this in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, at a breakfast meeting with media friends led by Elder Asu Beks. The meeting was themed, “Counting the Gains of the Oil Sector Reforms Under President Bola Tinubu.” The minister said Nigeria was producing less than one million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate when the Tinubu administration assumed office in 2023. He said production had since risen to 1.824 million barrels per day, including condensate, citing the latest weekly report of the Nigerian Upstream Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). “Condensate is not counted by OPEC. As of the last weekly report from NUPRC, we are producing 1,824,000 barrels per day inclusive of condensate. That is over 80 per cent from where we started in 2023,” he said. According to Lokpobiri, the increase was achieved through the concerted efforts of stakeholders in the oil and gas industry, under the leadership of the President. He said Nigeria previously had fewer than 10 active drilling rigs and had recorded no seismic activity for more than two decades. The minister said the number of active drilling rigs had now risen to more than 70, noting that drilling a well costs between $25 million and $30 million onshore and between $80 million and $100 million offshore. He also claimed that Nigeria, which he said recorded virtually no oil and gas investment for more than a decade before the Tinubu administration, now accounts for about 60 per cent of oil and gas investments coming into Africa. Lokpobiri attributed the development partly to the Federal Government’s approval of the divestments by Shell to Renaissance and ExxonMobil to Seplat. He said the approvals had unlocked investments in projects including the Bonga North, Bonga South-West and Zabazaba fields. The minister also said indigenous oil companies now accounted for about 60 per cent of Nigeria’s crude oil production, compared with the period when international oil companies produced about 90 per cent. Subsidy removal On the removal of petrol subsidy, Lokpobiri described the policy as inevitable, saying the Federal Government had previously spent about N18.4 billion daily on subsidy when the exchange rate was N448 to the dollar. He said the expenditure amounted to about $15 billion annually, or approximately N21 trillion when calculated at an exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar. The minister said the removal of the subsidy had also strengthened the revenue available for distribution to the three tiers of government through the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC). According to him, monthly FAAC allocations have increased from less than N600 billion to more than N2 trillion. He said the increase had enabled 27 states that previously struggled to pay salaries to meet their obligations and execute development projects. Lokpobiri said the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), which he claimed previously did not declare profits or meet cash-call obligations, now declares profits, contributes to the Federation Account and meets its financial obligations. He said Section 205 of the Petroleum Industry Act, signed into law by former President Muhammadu Buhari, provides for market-based pricing. The minister added that deregulation had enabled the Dangote Refinery to supply aviation fuel to European markets. According to him, Nigeria had previously been subsidising petrol consumption across parts of West and Central Africa before the subsidy was removed. Atala oil field Speaking on the disputed Atala oil field in Bayelsa State, Lokpobiri said the state government had challenged the matter in court but lost at both the Federal High Court and Court of Appeal. He said efforts were now being made to explore a political solution that would facilitate funding for the development of the field. On OML 240, which he said belonged to Bayelsa State, the minister said the oil block was awarded more than two decades ago and had since expired. He added that a Norwegian company had been brought in to develop the asset. The post Tinubu reforms raise oil output by 80% — Lokpobiri appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Four more die in Anambra communal clash, as govt shuts Otuocha Market
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Four more people have been confirmed dead, bringing the number to five, following a violent clash between Aguleri and Umuoba Anam communities in Anambra East local government area of Anambra State. The state Deputy Governor, Dr Onyekachukwu Ibezim, who visited the troubled area in company of the state Commissioner of Police, CP Nanna Oji Ama, directed the immediate suspension of economic and other activities in the market following the escalation of hostilities in the area. Several houses and shops were destroyed and in a viral video, voices were heard ordering armed men to shoot at sight. Many residents of the area have fled and the ever busy Otuocha-Umuoba Anam road has been deserted. Rice mills and hundreds of bags of rice were destroyed and smoke was seen coming out of many residential houses, while traders were seen salvaging some of their property. The cause The cause of the clash was said to be the alleged decision of Aguleri Community to mount a signpost and a Closed Circuit Television, CCTV, cameras on the boundary between the two communities, which Umuoba Anam Community resisted. Ibezim, who is the Chairman of Anambra State Boundary Committee, ordered that there should be no activity in the market until the state government completes necessary investigations and takes appropriate action against those responsible for the incident. He warned that no community leader or local government chairman has the authority to determine boundaries between communities without the knowledge of the state government, stressing that the State Boundary Committee is responsible for determining boundaries within the state. The traditional ruler of Aguleri, Igwe Mike Indigo and his Umuoba Anam counterpart, Igwe George Ekwealor, have, however, been appealing to their subjects to maintain peace and allow the government to handle the matter. Vanguard News The post Four more die in Anambra communal clash, as govt shuts Otuocha Market appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’actrice algérienne Hanaa Mansour accuse Kamel Daoud de violation du droit à l’image
items.description: Une actrice algérienne dénonce Kamel Daoud et le journal Le Point pour avoir associé son image, sans son consentement, à une chronique publiée le 30 septembre. La chronique est intitulée “ Monologue imaginaire d’une Franco-algérienne ”. Le journaliste-écrivain se met dans la peau d’une française d'origine algérienne qui raconte les déchirures de sa double nationalité et de sa double culture. Hanaa Mansour : « Je dénonce l'utilisation de mon image » par Kamel Daoud L’article est illustré sur les réseaux sociaux par une photo de l'actrice algérienne Hanaa Mansour qui, à l’évidence, n’a rien à voir avec la thématique abordée. “ Je dénonce l'utilisation de mon image, sans mon autorisation, dans le cadre d'un article publié par un média français portant sur l'Algérie ”, a écrit l’actrice dans un communiqué. Précisant qu’elle n’a été “ ni sollicitée ni consultée ” pour l'utilisation de sa photographie, Hanaa a indiqué qu’elle refuse que son image soit associée, “ de quelque manière que ce soit, au contenu ou à la ligne éditoriale de cet article ”. “ L'utilisation de mon image dans un contexte que je n'ai pas choisi et auquel je n'ai donné aucun accord constitue, à mes yeux, une atteinte à mon droit à l'image et à mon droit de contrôler l'utilisation de celle-ci ”, a-t-elle écrit. Tout en demandant “ le retrait immédiat ” de la photographie de l'article et de tout support lié à sa publication, l’actrice algérienne dit se réserver le droit d'engager “ toute démarche et action judiciaire ” qu’elle jugerait nécessaire afin de faire respecter ses droits. “Je n’ai rien à voir ni avec l’article ni avec l’écrivain” Elle a en outre fait une vidéo qu'elle a demandé à ses fans de partager sur les réseaux sociaux, assurant qu’elle n’a rien avoir ni avec l’article ni avec son auteur. Hanaa Mansour, 26 ans, est née et a grandi à Alger. Influenceuse sur les réseaux sociaux sous le pseudonyme de Rexleur, mannequin, est aussi actrice ayant apparu dans de nombreuses œuvres télévisuelles et cinématographiques, notamment la série “ Dama ” diffusée par la Télévision algérienne en 2023 et le film “ Première Ligne ” de Merzak Allouache (2024). Kamel Daoud est confronté depuis 2024 à des accusations de violation de la vie privée d'une victime algérienne du terrorisme. Saada Arbane a reconnu son histoire personnelle à travers le personnage Aube du roman “ Houris ” qui a valu à Daoud le prix Goncourt 2024. L'écrivain a été condamné par le tribunal d'Oran à 3 ans de prison ferme en avril dernier pour avoir repris l’histoire personnelle de Mme Arbane sans son consentement. L’article L’actrice algérienne Hanaa Mansour accuse Kamel Daoud de violation du droit à l’image est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 48-hour detention rule is not an automatic entitlement for EOCO – Victoria Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer and entrepreneur Victoria Bright has questioned the continued detention of Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), arguing that the constitutional 48-hour detention period should not be treated as an automatic entitlement for investigators. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 3, Ms Bright said EOCO must be able to explain the specific investigative purpose being served by keeping the MP in custody. “The 48-hour constitutional rule is there for a purpose. It’s there to safeguard against excessive detention, and we should not seem to now be treating it as a default entitlement of the state to detain everybody for 48 hours.” According to her, “if EOCO believes Baffour Awuah’s continued detention is necessary, the agency should explain what investigative purpose the detention serves and bring him before the court as soon as possible.” Her comments follow Baffour Awuah’s detention after he voluntarily reported himself to EOCO on October 1 to assist investigations into alleged financial offences involving SIC Life Savings and Loans. EOCO had earlier secured a High Court warrant for his arrest and searches of his office and residence. Ms Bright noted that the MP is a sitting legislator whose residence and constituency are known, and who had voluntarily presented himself to investigators. She argued that these circumstances should be considered when determining whether continued detention is necessary. EOCO had said it was working with the Attorney-General’s Office to bring the MP before a weekend court, citing applicable constitutional timelines and procedural requirements governing bail. Ms Bright’s comments come amid growing debate over the necessity and manner of Baffour Awuah’s detention, with his lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, also questioning why the MP was kept overnight after voluntarily reporting to EOCO.

Gunmen kill two at Plateau mining site
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Two persons from Heipang District in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State have been shot dead by suspected gunmen at a mining site around Kuru Jenta, near the boundary between Kuru Jenta in Jos South Local Government Area and Heipang. The incident, according to community sources, occurred at about 11:30pm on Friday when the victims were at the mining site. A member of the affected community, Weng Bulus, who confirmed the incident, condemned the killing and cautioned residents against engaging in mining activities at night. Bulus alleged that the victims were at the mining site during the period of the curfew imposed by the state government, urging residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements during restricted hours. She cautioned residents against violating the curfew, particularly by engaging in night mining, saying such movements could expose them to security risks. Bulus also condemned the attack and called on residents to take necessary precautions in view of the security situation in the area. Also reacting, spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the killing and called on security operatives to go after the attackers. Tengwong described the incident as unfortunate and urged security agencies to investigate the killing, identify those responsible and bring them to justice. He also cautioned residents, particularly miners, against engaging in night mining and urged them to remain vigilant and comply with security measures put in place by the government. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the latest incident were unsuccessful as of the time of sending this report. The post Gunmen kill two at Plateau mining site appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Baffour Awuah’s arrest is a political witch-hunt – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Lawyer and Senior Vice-President of IMANI Ghana, Kofi Bentil, has described the arrest of Manhyia South MP, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) as a political witch-hunt. Mr Bentil argued that the action against the legislator was politically motivated. He maintained that members of both the New Patriotic Party (NPP) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) knew that the arrest amounted to a political attack. “Look, let me say this. There is nobody I have come across, both in NPP, NDC or otherwise, who is not convinced that this is a political witch hunt,” “Even the NDC people know that this one we are going after the guy,” he said. “What is the charge? What has he been arrested for? What has he been accused of?. All that we heard is that he is deemed to have taken more than his proper fees and that he took it from both sides. I don’t understand what (EOCO) is saying.,” he added. Mr Bentil, who is also a business strategy lecturer and consultant, made the comments during discussions on the controversy surrounding EOCO’s handling of the case on JoyNews Newsfile on Saturday, October 3. His position differed from that of legal practitioner and NDC Communications Team member, Theophelious Dzimegah Jnr, who defended the agency on the same programme. Mr Dzimegah argued that EOCO was carrying out its legally mandated duties and had not violated the MP’s human rights. He maintained that Mr Baffour Awuah should have submitted himself to investigators, given his connection to the law firm involved in the transactions under investigation. The MP’s arrest followed a disputed attempt to take him into custody at the Accra High Court on September 23. EOCO said the action was intended to secure his attendance after earlier invitations were not honoured. His lawyers challenged that account, saying a representative of his law firm had already engaged with investigators and provided the information requested. Mr Baffour Awuah subsequently reported to EOCO on October 1 following a High Court arrest warrant and was placed under arrest. The investigation concerns alleged financial offences involving transactions connected to SIC Life Savings and Loans Company Limited. His legal team has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, maintaining that the firm provided legitimate legal services.

items.title: MT Asharami Ghana arrives in Tema as government pushes stronger LPG infrastructure
items.description: The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has stressed the need for strategic investments in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) infrastructure to strengthen Ghana’s energy security and expand access to cleaner energy. He said such investments were essential to Ghana’s energy future as the country sought to improve LPG availability for households and businesses while positioning itself as a regional energy and logistics hub. Dr Jinapor made the remarks at a reception ceremony in Tema to welcome the MT Asharami Ghana, a 40,000-cubic-metre LPG carrier with a cargo capacity of 5,000 metric tonnes of LPG. The vessel, purpose-built to serve Ghana and neighbouring markets, is expected to support efforts to improve LPG supply and enhance energy security across West Africa. “The arrival of MT Asharami Ghana represents a significant step forward in our quest to expand access to cleaner energy solutions for Ghanaians,” the Minister said. He commended Sahara Group for its contribution to Ghana’s energy sector, saying the government could not achieve its energy security and sustainable development objectives alone. “Government cannot achieve this vision alone. We commend Sahara Group for standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Ghana over the years in supporting our aspirations for energy security, economic growth and sustainable development,” he said. The Minister said the arrival of the vessel demonstrated the importance of collaboration between the government and private-sector players in developing the country’s energy infrastructure. Mr Wale Ajibade, Executive Director of Sahara Group, said the vessel represented a strategic investment in regional energy infrastructure, spanning shipping, storage and downstream distribution. He said the vessel’s maiden voyage to Ghana marked a significant step towards improving access to cleaner energy. “This maiden voyage to Ghanaian shores signals a resounding welcome to greater access to cleaner energy, healthier homes and communities, thriving businesses and a more sustainable environment,” he said. He said the investment reflected the Group’s confidence in Ghana’s potential and its commitment to working with stakeholders to provide sustainable energy solutions. “At Sahara, we see MT Asharami Ghana as a symbol of confidence in Ghana’s future. It reflects our unwavering belief in Ghana’s immense potential and our determination to work alongside stakeholders to deliver sustainable energy solutions that improve lives, create opportunities and drive inclusive growth,” he said. Ms Yaa Serwaa Alifo, Managing Director of Asharami Ghana, described the vessel’s arrival as a transformative moment for the company and Ghana’s energy sector. “What we are celebrating here is the culmination of a vision and a bold statement of our commitment to Ghana’s energy future,” she said. She said the vessel would improve access to cleaner fuel while strengthening supply reliability for households and businesses.

items.title: Weweso JHS wins 5th edition of Otumfuo Reading Competition 2026
items.description: A pupil of Weweso M/A JHS, Joycelyn Akosua Manu Duah, has emerged as the winner of the 5th edition of the Otumfuo Community Reading Challenge. Originally the Oduom champion of the competition, Joycelyn Akosua Manu Duah placed first ahead of four other finalists who competed for the ultimate prize in the annual reading competition. Joycelyn secured 95.2 points at the grand finale held at the Manhyia Palace in Kumasi. Stephanie Agyiewaa, who is the Duayaw Nkwanta champion from Yamfo Methodist School, lost the title by a slimmer margin, placing second with 95.1 points. Twedie champion, Magdalene Duodu Akwabeng from Manuel International School, finished third with 94.3 points, while Obuasi champion, Randy Boakye Yiadom, from Bodomase St. Stephen R/C JHS followed the pack with 92.9 points. Meanwhile, Samuel Opoku Kyeremah, the Barekese champion from Adankwame D/A JHS, trailed the contest with 91.0 points. The Otumfuo Community Reading Challenge was established by the Otumfuo Foundation to promote reading, improve literacy and encourage students to develop their reading and comprehension skills. The 2026 competition marked its fifth edition, bringing together outstanding student readers from different communities to compete at the grand finale. As part of her prize package, Joycelyn will receive an Otumfuo Foundation scholarship to university, a GH¢10,000 cash prize, as well as souvenirs from sponsors. Joycelyn expressed her profound gratitude to her school and supporters for the achievement and a special appreciation to the Asantehene for the initiative. She encouraged her peers to leverage the opportunity to excel in academics. “I urged all fellow students to take their studies seriously and remain focused on their education,” she added. Otumfuo Hiahene, Nana Prof. Oheneba Baochie-Adjei, commended the initiative and called for continued investment in reading and education among young people. He said initiatives such as the Otumfuo Community Reading Challenge are important in nurturing a strong reading culture and developing the intellectual abilities of young people. Nana Prof. Oheneba further highlighted how articulating one’s thoughts in both the local dialect, Asante Twi, and English is helpful in bridging the gap between indigenous and modern culture. “The students do not just read in our local dialect, but it helps them to know more about the history and culture of the Asantes,” he said.

items.title: ‘Criminal law can’t turn every poor commercial judgment involving state entity into an offence’ – Victoria Bright
items.description: International corporate lawyer and entrepreneur Victoria Bright has cautioned against automatically treating the controversial SIC Life settlement at the centre of the Economic and Organised Crime Office’s (EOCO) investigation into Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah as a criminal matter. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile, she said the fact that a commercial settlement involving a state entity may subsequently appear unwise does not, on its own, establish criminal conduct. Her comments come as EOCO investigates Baffour Awuah over alleged criminal conspiracy, financial loss to SIC Savings and Loans, money laundering, tax-related offences and other matters. The MP voluntarily reported himself to EOCO on October 1 after the High Court issued a warrant for his arrest and authorised searches linked to the investigation. The investigation includes questions surrounding a settlement reached in a matter involving SIC Life Savings and Loans and Equity Savings and Loans, where the amount originally invested by SIC had increased substantially with accrued interest before a settlement was reached. Victoria Bright said investigators must establish whether the settlement was properly authorised and examine the documentation surrounding the transaction, including who approved the settlement and what instructions were given to the lawyers. She stressed that “a bad settlement is not automatically a crime”, arguing that commercial decisions can sometimes prove unwise without necessarily constituting criminal offences. “So these commercial decisions are made all the time, and criminal law can’t turn every poor exercise of commercial judgment involving a state entity into an offense. We need to be careful.” At the same time, she cautioned that describing a transaction as a settlement cannot shield an arrangement that is otherwise shown by evidence to be unlawful. Her position is that the investigation should therefore focus on the evidence and the authority behind the transaction, rather than assuming either criminality or political persecution.

items.title: ‘Tinubu’s reforms working; we want to remain worthy partners’ – Akpabio
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration reforms, saying they are yielding good result, and that the National Assembly wants to maintain partnership with him. Read Also: How Nigeria declined into criminality, poor governance in 66 years The Senate President led a high-level delegation from the National Assembly, featuring Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Benjamin Kalu, that visited President Bola Tinubu in his Lagos home on Friday to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. He declared full legislative partnership with the administration and insisting that insecurity is abating despite “pockets of discontent”. Speaking to journalists after the visit, Akpabio, who chairs the National Assembly, said the delegation came “to pay a visit to Nigeria through the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces”. “We are happy with the fact that Nigeria has met 66 years. So we came to pay a visit to Nigeria through the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces,” Akpabio said. “We believe he’s doing well. These reforms are working and, as far as we are concerned, insecurities are abating and people are able to sleep well,” he added. Acknowledges challenges The Senate President acknowledged lingering challenges but attributed some to the proximity of elections. “We still have pockets of discontent here and there because of the fact that this is almost election time. A lot of mischief and all that. “But at the end, our prayer always is that Nigeria shall be better, and God will help him to make Nigeria, beyond 66 years, a better country,” Akpabio said. He framed Nigeria’s continued unity as evidence of divine favour and national resilience. “That we are still together shows the resilience of this country. That Nigeria is still one. It shows the resilience of this country. It shows the love that God has for Nigeria,” he said. “We are a praying nation. Whether you are a Muslim or you are a Christian, we are a praying nation. And God can never forsake us. And God will never forsake the President,” Akpabio stated. On the administration’s performance, he said: “So the administration is doing its best, considering the situation we took when we came about. And we are prepared and determined to make the country better.” Pledges legislative support for President Tinubu “On the part of the National Assembly, we want to continue to remain worthy partners to the administration of President Bola Tinubu. And we believe that what we are doing is in the interest of all Nigerians,” he said. He cited the reversal to the old national anthem as a symbol of unity. “Even from when we changed the national anthem to what it is today, and what it was then at independence, it’s a clear reflection of the love we have for Nigeria: that though tongues and tribes may differ, in brotherhood we stand,” Akpabio said. “Nigerians must learn to be their brother’s keepers once more, and love must return to Nigeria. And progress is already on the trajectory. Things are changing,” he added. Responding to a question on how the National Assembly is partnering with the executive to reduce the cost of living, Akpabio pointed to recent overhauls of colonial-era laws, particularly in taxation. “You’ve seen already, in three years, we have been able to tinker with all the anachronistic and old laws that we met on the ground. You know very well that things like stamp duties were laws that were in 1939. “And some of the laws were incorporated in 1901. And the laws of 1959 were incorporated into the Nigerian Constitution, the current one we are having. And many of them have not been changed,” he said. “Stamp duties, so many others. So you’ve seen the reform in the tax system. Let me use the word economic system, with four major tax laws brought into the country at one time. Very voluminous, all of them. And then, because we’re able to digest them, we’re able to do what we ought to do,” Akpabio stated. He said the laws were passed quickly and with broad support. “And we’re able to pass them in record time with the whole country in agreement. At the beginning, people were very sceptical and said, ‘What are they trying to do? Are they trying to make a law for one section or the other?’ We say we are all for all Nigeria. It’s a people’s parliament and we are doing that,” he said. Akpabio urged Nigerians to judge the government by results. “You’ve seen the speed with which we pass legislations that benefit Nigeria. You’ve seen the speed that we clear people who are coming to add value to the current administration. “You’ve seen the partnership in terms of laws that definitely will change the paradigm of the Nigerian trajectory,” he said. “And so we will continue to do that. That’s our own contribution. We are elected for that and we partner with an administration which we believe is focused and which is determined to change the fortunes of Nigeria,” Akpabio added. “Don’t forget, it’s easy to say with the mouth, but difficult to do. But in our own case, we are matching words with action. And so the government is going forward,” he concluded. Vanguard News The post ‘Tinubu’s reforms working; we want to remain worthy partners’ – Akpabio appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Inculpé pour faux monnayage et place sous contrôle judiciaire : Reug Reug entre arène et justice
items.description: Sans rien ôter à son parcours exceptionnel, Oumar Kane dit « Reug Reug », a su s’imposer comme une figure incontournable de la lutte sans frappe. En lutte avec frappe, il s’est bâti un solide palmarès avant de s’illustrer dans le monde des arts martiaux mixtes (MMA). Sacré champion du monde des poids lourds du One Championship en novembre 2024 après sa victoire contre Anatoly Malykhin, il a cédé sa ceinture face à ce même adversaire le 15 mai 2026. Quelques mois plus tôt, le 7 janvier 2026, il avait renoué avec le succès dans l’arène sénégalaise en terrassant Boy Niang 2. Pourtant, le champion traverse aujourd’hui de sombres déboires judiciaires après son inculpation et son placement sous contrôle judiciaire. Retour sur cette affaire de faux billets qui menace d’assombrir sa carrière sportive, notamment son combat contre Franc, prévu le 31 janvier 2027. Inculpé par le juge du 3ᵉ cabinet du Tribunal de grande instance de Dakar pour association de malfaiteurs, tentative d’escroquerie et détention de matières destinées à la contrefaçon de billets de banque ayant cours légal, le lutteur Oumar Kane, alias Reug Reug, échappe pour le moment à la prison. Arrêté aux Maristes par la Brigade de recherches de Faidherbe en compagnie de son oncle, Ahmadou Bamba Ndiaye, et du « Saltigué » Diégane Faye, le trio était en possession de billets noirs de 100 dollars, d’une valeur estimée à 830 millions de FCfa. Déférés au parquet le lundi 28 septembre, ils ont d’abord fait l’objet d’un retour de parquet. Le lendemain, mardi 29 septembre 2026, le juge d’instruction a prononcé leur inculpation pour les chefs d’accusation susmentionnés. Parcours élogieux d’un champion Cependant, le magistrat n’a pas suivi le réquisitoire du ministère public concernant le lutteur : s’il l’a bel et bien inculpé, il l’a placé sous contrôle judiciaire avec remise en liberté. Une clémence dont n’ont pas bénéficié ses deux co-prévenus, placés, eux, sous mandat de dépôt. L’affaire a toutefois connu un nouveau rebondissement le 30 septembre 2026. Le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de grande instance de Dakar a interjeté appel contre la décision de mise en liberté sous contrôle judiciaire. Le sort de Reug Reug est désormais entre les mains de la chambre d’accusation de la Cour d’appel de Dakar, qui doit se prononcer sur le recours du parquet. Si la chambre infirme la décision du juge d’instruction, le lutteur risque un placement sous mandat de dépôt. Oumar Kane dit « Reug Reug », a connu les sommets, mais aussi les épreuves qui forgent les vrais champions. Né à Thiaroye-sur-Mer, il a très tôt appris à se battre pour s’imposer. Marqué par le décès prématuré de son père, Diagar Kane, c’est son oncle paternel, Aladji Kane, qui prend alors la famille en charge. C’est d’ailleurs ce dernier qui lui attribue le surnom de « Reug Reug », inspiré d’un personnage d’un téléfilm diffusé sur la RTS. Pour le jeune Oumar, la lutte est une véritable hérédité. Son grand-père paternel, Modou Kane, comme son grand-père maternel, Modou Diène, étaient tous deux lutteurs. Son père avait lui aussi pratiqué la discipline, parallèlement au football. Le destin du champion semblait donc tracé d’avance : il ne pouvait échapper à l’arène, même si la pêche, profondément ancrée dans son identité léboue, reste intimement liée à son histoire. Confié au manager Palla Diop en 2010, Reug Reug est d’abord orienté vers la lutte sans frappe, l’absence de pièce d’identité et diverses contraintes administratives l’empêchant alors d’obtenir une licence de lutte avec frappe. Dans cette discipline, il se forge une solide réputation en accumulant les titres et les drapeaux pendant plusieurs années. Ses débuts en lutte avec frappe s’avèrent plus modestes. Le 25 décembre 2011, il affronte Clinton de Walo. Le verdict initial, contesté par son camp, est finalement cassé par la Commission des règlements et de la discipline de l’ancien Comité national de gestion (CNG) de lutte, qui le transforme en « sans-verdict ». Reug Reug enchaîne ensuite les succès : Alioune Sèye Jr, Boy Niague 2, Boy Diouf, Obama, Sa Ngoumbeu, Bazooka bou Ngoye, Fall Yarakh, Balla Gaye Jr, Brise-de-Mer, Bébé Saloum, Jordan, Elton, Gris 2 puis Gouye Gui tombent successivement sous ses coups. Sa seule défaite concédée dans l’arène survient le 5 mars 2023 face à Sa Thiès. La conquête du monde avec le Mma Le Géant de Thiaroye rebondit rapidement en s’offrant l’ancien Roi des arènes, Bombardier, le 24 décembre 2023, avant de confirmer son rang face à Boy Niang 2, le 7 juin 2026. Une victoire majeure qui scelle son retour au sommet parmi les ténors dits « Vip » de l’arène. Parallèlement au « sport de chez nous », Reug Reug s’est lancé dans les arts martiaux mixtes (MMA). Révélé lors de l’évènement Ares 1, organisé à Dakar en décembre 2019, il rejoint rapidement le One Championship. Le 22 janvier 2021, il y réussit ses débuts en s’imposant face au Camerounais Alain Ngalani. Son ascension internationale atteint son apothéose le 8 novembre 2024 : opposé au colosse russe Anatoly Malykhin, il l’emporte aux points par décision partagée et devient le premier Sénégalais à décrocher le titre de champion du monde poids lourds du One Championship. Mais le sport de haut niveau ne pardonne rien. Le 15 mai 2026, à Bangkok (Thaïlande), les deux hommes se retrouvent pour un combat revanche. Cette fois, le Russe l’emporte par arrêt de l’arbitre au quatrième round et récupère sa ceinture mondiale. Reug Reug concède ainsi la deuxième défaite de sa carrière en neuf combats de MMA. Toutefois, ce revers ne saurait résumer son parcours exceptionnel. De Thiaroye et des tournois de « mbapatt » jusqu’aux plus grandes arènes internationales du MMA, Reug Reug a constamment fait étalage de son talent, de sa détermination et du courage d’un véritable lion. La quête se poursuit : le champion entend bien écrire de nouvelles pages de sa légende. Par Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: Incident Flydubai : la RAM affirme avoir écarté la candidature du copilote
items.description: La Royal Air Maroc (RAM) a réagi officiellement à des informations selon lesquelles le copilote impliqué dans l'incident du vol Flydubai aurait auparavant travaillé au sein de la compagnie nationale. Ce dernier n'aurait pas été retenu pour travailler au sein de la RAM. Suite à des informations relayées par certains médias selon lesquelles le copilote impliqué dans l'incident du vol Flydubai aurait auparavant travaillé pour Royal Air Maroc, la compagnie nationale « précise que l'intéressé avait effectué en 2025, en son sein, une formation théorique de trois mois, préalable à une éventuelle embauc he ». Cependant, « à l'issue de cette formation, sa candidature avait été écartée » , indique Royal Air Maroc dans un communiqué. Dans le même temps, l'enquête menée par les autorités émiraties sur l'incident du vol l FZ1073 de Flydubai, a révélé que le co-pilote « avait entreprise de commettre un acte terroriste », selon le conseiller Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, procureur général de la Fédération, cité par l'agence WAM. Le procureur général a expliqué que le copilote aurait commencé à mettre son plan à exécution pendant le vol, en agressant le commandant de bord à l’intérieur du cockpit à l’aide de la hache de secours (Crash Axe) et aurait tenté de prendre le contrôle des commandes de l’avion. Hamad Saif Al Shamsi a indiqué que les investigations, notamment l’examen des preuves matérielles et numériques, se poursuivent pour déterminer toutes les circonstances de l'incident, et les résultats définitifs seront annoncés dès l’achèvement des procédures. The post Incident Flydubai : la RAM affirme avoir écarté la candidature du copilote appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Baffour Awuah has shown willingness to cooperate, qualifies for self-recognisance bail – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Lawyer and Senior Vice President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, says Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah qualifies to be granted bail on his own recognisance, arguing that the lawmaker has demonstrated his willingness to cooperate with investigators. Mr Bentil said the Manhyia South MP’s decision to voluntarily report himself to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) should be considered in determining whether he poses any risk of absconding or interfering with the investigation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 3, he said self-recognisance bail was generally appropriate where an accused person was considered unlikely to flee and was willing to submit to the investigative process. “You know there is self-recognisance bail. And the principle of self-recognisance bail is that the person is not a flight risk and that the person will submit themselves to the investigative processes,” he said. Mr Bentil said the arrangement was often considered for people whose public profile and circumstances made it unlikely that they would abscond. “It’s usually given to people who are public figures, easily recognizable, you know what they are doing and they really don’t have an incentive not to cooperate,” he said. He argued that parliamentarians, by virtue of their public responsibilities and visibility, would ordinarily have little incentive to flee. “If there are any group of people who are qualified for self-recognisance bail, it will be parliamentarians,” he said. Mr Bentil also pointed to Mr Baffour Awuah’s decision to voluntarily report to EOCO as evidence of his willingness to cooperate with the investigation. “And in this particular situation somebody who actually submitted himself, somebody you claim you have been pursuing since February is notoriously public, is in court representing people, is in parliament doing his work,” he said. He questioned whether the MP had any incentive to abandon his parliamentary duties and constituency to evade investigators. “Is there a single incentive, even half an incentive for him to abandon his constituency and flee? Because you are charging him with something we all don’t understand,” he said. Mr Bentil therefore argued that he saw no justification for keeping the MP in custody rather than granting him bail. “The point I want to make first is that there is absolutely no reason I can find for not giving Honorable Baffour Awuah bail. He qualifies for self-recognizance bail,” he said. “He clearly has shown that he will walk to the place. He doesn’t have an incentive not to participate in the investigation etc.” Mr Baffour Awuah voluntarily reported to EOCO on Thursday, October 1, to assist with investigations into transactions involving SIC Life Savings and Loans and was subsequently detained by the agency. The development followed an earlier attempt by EOCO to arrest the MP at the Accra High Court Complex on September 23, an incident that has generated debate over the manner in which the agency sought to execute the arrest.

items.title: IWT’s future
items.description: TOGETHER with the Kashmir dispute, India’s unilateral suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty has become the biggest source of bilateral friction in the subcontinent. In a controversial move, New Delhi held the decades-old agreement ‘in abeyance’ in 2025 after the Pahalgam episode . But as Pakistan’s senior leadership has highlighted, Indian brinkmanship in this regard may set a negative precedent globally, while also planting the seeds of a new conflict in South Asia. Speaking at an event in Islamabad the other day, Information Minister Atta Tarar said that India’s unilateral action vis-à-vis the IWT could threaten global water governance . He termed New Delhi’s moves “morally bankrupt and devoid of ethics”. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had raised the issue earlier, when he addressed the UN General Assembly last week. He did not mince his words when he said that diverting Pakistan’s water would amount to an “act of war” . This is not mere rhetoric. The Indus and its tributaries are Pakistan’s lifeline, and the country cannot allow India to blackmail it using these precious waters. India has ruled out restoring the treaty until Pakistan acts against ‘cross-border terrorism’. This is a weak alibi being deployed to take what belongs to Pakistan. New Delhi has remained adamant despite the ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in August that the IWT could not be unilaterally suspended. India has brushed aside the court’s decision. Along with the key issue of water rights, the larger question is what sort of precedent India wants to set. Its leaders speak of multilateralism and the global ‘rules-based order’. Yet in practice, when they scupper bilateral treaties and refuse to recognise decisions by respected arbitrators, the Indians in fact promote the law of the jungle. Pakistan must continue to pursue its legitimate rights with regard to the Indus waters. It must also point out the double standards India adheres to — claiming to uphold global norms, yet trampling on international law. If the IWT dispute is left to fester, or worse, if India takes further steps to cut off Pakistan’s share of water, a new conflict in South Asia is quite possible. In order to avoid such a grim scenario, saner elements in India must work towards restoring the IWT, and addressing all other outstanding issues in a civilised manner. Published in Dawn, October 3rd, 2026

items.title: Guinea grants opposition figure Aliou Bah presidential pardon
items.description: Guinean opposition politician Aliou Bah, who was jailed for insulting junta leader General Mamadi Doumbouya, was granted a presidential pardon Friday after nearly two years behind bars. The move frees one of the west African nation’s key opposition figures at a time when rights groups and political opponents have accused Guinea’s military rulers of tightening their grip on dissent since seizing power in 2021. Doumbouya granted pardons to 217 prisoners to mark Guinea’s independence day, according to a presidential decree read on state television by presidency secretary-general Amara Camara. Bah was among those named. Bah, head of the Liberal Democratic Movement (Model), had been detained since December 2024. He was sentenced in January last year. His release had not been expected until around December this year after being sentenced to two years for “offending and insulting” the head of state. An appeals court upheld the sentence in May 2025 despite prosecutors seeking a five-year prison term. Bah was convicted over remarks in which he called on Guinean religious leaders to “break their silence” about the country’s political situation and described the ruling National Committee of Rally for Development (CNRD) as “incompetent”. His case had also reached the Court of Justice of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). In a letter dated September 25, the regional court asked Guinea’s Supreme Court to order Bah’s immediate and unconditional release. Doumbouya seized power in September 2021 after overthrowing president Alpha Conde, Guinea’s first democratically elected leader. He strengthened his hold on power after winning a December 2025 presidential election that was not contested by any major opposition challenger. Opposition parties have accused the military authorities of systematically restricting political freedoms. Several major political parties have been dissolved, demonstrations have been banned or dispersed by security forces, and a number of government critics have been arrested, convicted, forced into exile or have disappeared. items.title: Gaza avant et après 2023 : Google Earth dévoile l’ampleur des destructions israéliennes
items.description: Malgré une communication prétendument rodée et les tentatives régulières de couvrir ses exactions dans sa guerre totale contre les Palestiniens, Israël se fait toujours rattraper par une réalité qu’il lui est difficile de dissimuler : sous le prétexte de traquer le mouvement Hamas, il s'est livré à une entreprise de destruction massive qui n'a épargné ni les vies humaines, ni les infrastructures, ni les habitations et ni les champs agricoles à Gaza . C'est en tous cas ce que montrent les images satellites. Devenues virales ces derniers jours, les vues de Gaza disponibles sur Google Earth et Google Maps donnent à voir l’ampleur des ravages et l’étendue des dégâts infligés par Israël à l’enclave palestinienne. Google Earth exposes devastation in Gaza with new updated images. Satellite images show the scale of devastation near Al-Qadisiyah School in Rafah, comparing the area in May 2022 with its condition in 2026 during the war on Gaza. pic.twitter.com/RafYrHnG9z — Eye on Palestine (@EyeonPalestine) October 2, 2026 Des millions d’internautes ont ainsi découvert des quartiers entiers rasés, réduits à des amas de gravats, des routes éventrées et des infrastructures totalement endommagées. Gaza avant et après 2023 : Israël a tout rasé à Gaza Partagées sur X par l’eurodéputé irlandais Barry Andrews, des captures d’écran montrant notamment Rafah, au sud de l'enclave, près de la frontière égyptienne, ont été vues plus de sept millions de fois. Le député les a qualifiées d’« assez incroyables ». Mises à jour par Google en juin, les images permettent de mesurer visuellement les transformations du territoire entre 2023, début de la guerre après l’attaque du mouvement Hamas, et 2026. À Tal al-Sultan, dans l’ouest de Rafah, les vues de 2026 montrent qu’il ne reste que quelques bâtiments debout là où s’étendait encore, quelques années auparavant, un tissu urbain dense. Le même contraste apparaît à l’est de Jabaliya, dans le nord de la bande de Gaza. Les images de juillet 2023 montrent des habitations entourées de bosquets. En 2026, la végétation a presque disparu, laissant place à des étendues de sable et de décombres. Seules quelques rares structures apparaissent encore debout. À Gaza-ville, les alentours de l’hôpital al-Chifa apparaissent eux aussi profondément transformés. Des bâtiments ont disparu et des espaces qui avaient d’autres fonctions-stade, carrefours ou ronds-points-sont devenus des lieux d’installation pour des populations déplacées, avec des rangées de tentes et d’abris de fortune. À Rafah, des spécialistes de l’imagerie satellitaire, repris par de nombreux médias occidentaux, ont décrit une destruction particulièrement importante dans plusieurs secteurs, notamment à Tal al-Sultan. Les images donnent à voir un décor et une métamorphose du territoire qui n’ont rien à envier à ceux des destructions qui ont marqué la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Guerre contre Gaza : un bilan effarant Au-delà des images satellites, le bilan établi par les institutions internationales donne une mesure beaucoup plus précise de cette dévastation. Le dernier Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment (RDNA), réalisé conjointement par la Banque mondiale, l’ONU et l’Union européenne, datant d’avril dernier, estime à 35,2 milliards de dollars les dommages physiques enregistrés dans la bande de Gaza jusqu’en octobre 2025. Les pertes économiques et sociales sont, elles, évaluées à 22,7 milliards de dollars, portant l’impact cumulé à près de 58 milliards de dollars. Les besoins de reconstruction et de relèvement sont encore plus considérables : 71,4 milliards de dollars sur dix ans, dont 26,3 milliards nécessaires au cours des dix-huit premiers mois, selon le rapport. Le secteur du logement concentre à lui seul environ 18 milliards de dollars de dommages. Près de 372 000 logements, soit plus des trois quarts du parc, ont été détruits ou endommagés. Plus d’un million de personnes ont perdu leur logement. L’éducation a également été frappée de plein fouet. Près de 95 % des établissements scolaires avaient été endommagés ou détruits à la fin de 2025 selon l’Unicef, tandis que des centaines de milliers d’enfants ont été privés d’enseignement formel. Le secteur de la santé n’a pas été épargné, non plus. Au moment de l’évaluation, moins de la moitié des hôpitaux et moins de 38 % des centres de soins primaires étaient encore partiellement fonctionnels. Les infrastructures d’eau et d’assainissement, les routes, l’énergie, les télécommunications et les terres agricoles ont également subi des dégâts considérables. La destruction dépasse ainsi largement les seuls bâtiments résidentiels. Elle touche les réseaux essentiels à la survie de la population palestinienne. Destruction de Gaza : complicité occidentale avec Israël Lorsqu’il avait été cloué au pilori par des organismes internationaux et fortement critiqué par certaines ONG au vu de l’ampleur des destructions sans ménagement, Israël avait répliqué que ses opérations avaient pour objectif de démanteler les infrastructures du Hamas, d’éliminer ses combattants et d’empêcher son retour. Mais les images satellites de Google Earth conjuguées à l’évaluation conjointe de la Banque mondiale, de l’ONU et de l’Union européenne montrent désormais une dévastation d’une ampleur telle qu’elle ne peut soutenir les arguments militaires avancés. À tous points de vue, il s'agit bel et bien d'une entreprise génocidaire que certaines puissances occidentales, par complicité ou complaisance, refusent de voir. L’article Gaza avant et après 2023 : Google Earth dévoile l’ampleur des destructions israéliennes est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Pakistan summons Indian envoy over killing of 2 civilians by border troops
items.description: Pakistan summoned the Indian chargé d’affaires to lodge a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday. Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s BSF near the border in Kasur on Friday. “The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked and lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives,” the FO said. Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as “infiltrators”, it added. The FO said the incident constituted a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised concerns over the protection of civilian life under international law. It called on the Indian side to “conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation”, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the government of Pakistan. India was further urged to “respect fundamental human rights and international law, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint in such situations, and take effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future”, the FO said. The three civilians were residents of Ladhar village and had moved a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF opened fire on them without warning. All three were unarmed. The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar. The injured civilian was taken for medical treatment. According to security sources, none of the three men had attempted to cross the border fence, with the incident described as a violation of the border agreement and standard operating procedures governing the international border. The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference. Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.

items.title: 2027: If fuel comes down to ₦600 tomorrow, I will campaign for Tinubu — Amaechi
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Vice Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has challenged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu over his economic policies, saying he will campaign for him in 2027 if petrol comes down to ₦600 per litre. Amaechi issued the challenge while reacting to Tinubu’s Independence Day speech and his declaration that Nigeria had entered an “age of prosperity”, during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today. Questioning the believability of the President’s claim, Amaechi challenged Tinubu to demonstrate that Nigerians are already experiencing the promised economic improvement. “It is about believability; who do you believe? Go to the 2005 Presidential speech; it is the same: we have turned the page, and we are about to start enjoyment,” Amaechi said. “Have you asked one of your staff who goes by transport, how much it costs from Yanya to Abuja? Has anything come down? “Has any price come down, has anything changed?” he asked. Amaechi then used the price of petrol as a test, saying he would personally visit a filling station to establish whether the price had fallen to ₦600. “I will go tomorrow morning to the petrol station to buy fuel, I will go myself, if fuel has come down to 600, I will campaign for President Tinubu. “If fuel comes down to 600 tomorrow, I will campaign for Tinubu,” he said. He further challenged those who doubted him to accompany him with a camera, insisting that he would withdraw from Atiku Abubakar’s ticket and campaign for Tinubu if the price had dropped to ₦600. “If you doubt me, come with your camera to my house, and I will go to the filling station and buy fuel, and I, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi will withdraw as a vice presidential candidate of Atiku and campaign for President Tinubu, if it has come down,” he added. The comments come as political parties and their candidates position themselves ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with Amaechi on the ADC ticket alongside former Vice presdient Atiku Abubakar. items.title: EOCO is only carrying out its mandate, not violating Baffour Awuah’s rights – Dzimegah
items.description: Legal practitioner and member of the NDC Communications Team, Theophelious Dzimegah Jnr, has defended the Economic and Organised Crime Office’s (EOCO) handling of its investigation involving Manhyia South MP, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah. Mr Dzimegah argued that EOCO was performing its legally mandated duties and had not violated the legislator’s human rights. He maintained that the MP should have submitted himself to investigators, given his leadership role at the law firm connected to the transactions under investigation. In Mr Dzimegah’s view, EOCO was justified in seeking the MP’s cooperation to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged financial offences, including money laundering. “I believe that, to a large extent, EOCO is doing its mandate. If you read Article 14 (3), it talks about when the person should be brought to court,” “So as it is now, I don’t think that EOCO has violated his (the MP) rights, it is not the use of power, but it is what it is that the investigative body needs to do,” he said on JoyNews Newsfile on Saturday, October 3. His comments come amid controversy over the agency’s attempts to secure Mr Baffour Awuah’s attendance and his subsequent arrest and detention. EOCO officers attempted to arrest the MP at the Accra High Court on September 23, 2026. The legislator resisted the move, describing it as an unlawful arrest and an attempted kidnapping, before seeking sanctuary at Parliament. EOCO said it had previously issued two invitations in February, which he had not honoured. However, his lawyers disputed that account. They said the correspondence concerned his capacity as Senior Partner of Sarkodie, Baffour Awuah and Partners and an investigation involving the firm’s client, SIC Life Savings and Loans Company Limited. According to the lawyers, a representative of the firm attended interrogation sessions on March 4, March 18 and April 30, and submitted a written statement to EOCO. The High Court subsequently issued an arrest warrant on September 30 after EOCO said it had exhausted reasonable means of securing the MP’s voluntary attendance. Mr Baffour Awuah reported to the agency on October 1 and was placed under arrest. EOCO later said he was cooperating with investigators. His counsel, Samuel Atta Akyea, said EOCO had presented charges including money laundering and causing financial loss to the state. He rejected the allegations, arguing that the transactions arose from legitimate legal services provided to recover an investment for SIC Life. In an update on October 2, EOCO said it was working with the Attorney-General’s Office to bring the MP before a weekend court within the applicable constitutional and procedural requirements. It also dismissed reports that he had been granted GH¢50 million bail.

items.title: Heavy security at Baba Yara Stadium as NPP elects national officers today
items.description: The Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi is under heavy security as the New Patriotic Party (NPP) prepares to elect its national executives today, Saturday, October 3. Hundreds of police officers are currently deployed within and around the stadium, with extensive security arrangements in place ahead of the arrival of delegates for the National Delegates Conference. NPP Organisation Committee Chairperson, Anthony Abayifaa Karbo, earlier disclosed that between 3,000 and 4,000 police personnel would be deployed to Kumasi to provide security for the conference and elections. He said the officers would be responsible for traffic management, securing hotels and hostels where delegates and guests are staying, as well as providing security around and inside the Baba Yara Sports Stadium. Mr Karbo commended the Inspector-General of Police and the Ashanti Regional Police Command for their cooperation in the preparations. Meanwhile, the main stage has been set for the conference, with public address systems and other facilities being put in place ahead of the programme. About 7,100 delegates are expected to participate in the elections, which will be supervised by the Electoral Commission (EC). The elections will produce the party’s national executives for the next phase of its internal organisation as the NPP prepares for the 2028 general election. The party has established 31 voting centres within the stadium to facilitate the exercise and prevent voting from extending late into the night. The EC says all electoral materials, including ballot papers, are ready, while accredited agents of the various candidates will observe the process. The conference will begin with constitutional and other party business before voting commences. A total of 46 candidates remain on the final ballot following the withdrawal of National Youth Organiser Salam Mustapha from the National Organiser race. The positions being contested include National Chairperson, Vice-Chairpersons, General Secretary, National Treasurer, National Organiser, National Youth Organiser, National Women’s Organiser and National Nasara Organiser. Dennis Miracles Aboagye is the sole candidate for National Communications Director. The elections form part of the NPP’s broader reorganisation, following the completion of polling station, electoral area, constituency and regional-level elections.
