items.title: Un financement japonais : plus de 2 milliards MRO pour soutenir la formation, l’encadrement agricole et l’aide alimentaire
items.description: Le ministre des Affaires économiques et du Développement, Abdallahi Ould Souleimane Ould Cheikh Sidiya, a signé vendredi, avec l’ambassadeur du Japon en Mauritanie, Hiroyuki Ocheda, deux accords de financement d’un montant total de 800 millions de yens japonais, soit environ 203 millions de nouvelles ouguiyas (2,03 milliards d’anciennes ouguiyas), destinés à soutenir la formation et l’encadrement agricoles ainsi que l’aide alimentaire. Le ministère des Affaires économiques et du Développement a indiqué que la première subvention, d’un montant de 400 millions de yens, doit contribuer à la mise en œuvre d’un programme de développement économique et social, par la fourniture d’équipements et de machines agricoles modernes ainsi que de matériel pédagogique au profit des établissements de formation et de vulgarisation agricole et professionnelle situés sur la rive du fleuve Sénégal. Le ministère a ajouté que la deuxième subvention, d’un montant de 400 millions de yens, octroyée dans le cadre du programme d’aide alimentaire, sera destinée à soutenir les projets générateurs de revenus, à reconstituer les stocks stratégiques nationaux de céréales, à renforcer la capacité du marché à assurer un approvisionnement régulier et à stabiliser les prix des produits de première nécessité. Le ministre des Affaires économiques et du Développement a souligné que ces deux accords témoignent de la profondeur et de la solidité des relations d’amitié et de coopération entre la Mauritanie et le Japon, précisant que la coopération entre les deux pays a connu un développement remarquable ces dernières années et a porté notamment sur les domaines de la pêche, de la santé, de l’éducation, de la formation professionnelle et de l’environnement.

items.title: Health Minister orders deployment of 40 additional health workers to Weija Children’s Specialist Hospital
items.description: Health Minister, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has directed the immediate deployment of 10 medical doctors and 30 nurses and midwives to the Weija Children’s Specialist Hospital. The move is aimed at strengthening the facility’s workforce as it expands its services as a specialist referral centre. Mr Akandoh gave the directive after inspecting the 120-bed hospital, which he said is now operational. He said the facility is currently providing outpatient and emergency services and is upgrading its operations to include inpatient care. “I have directed that with immediate effect, they should bring an additional 10 medical doctors and 30 nurses and midwives to beef up the health workforce. This is a referral centre, and I think it is the first of its kind as a stand-alone children’s referral centre,” he said. The Minister said most of the equipment required at the facility had been installed, allowing management to expand the range of services being offered. He also urged management and health workers to maintain the facility properly and ensure patients are treated with dignity and respect. “We have also impressed upon them to make sure they keep the facility well, maintain it and try to treat the patients with respect and dignity,” he said. Mr Akandoh said the Ministry was closely monitoring the hospital because of its importance to the country and was committed to ensuring that it becomes fully operational. “What Ghanaians wanted to see is that this facility is in full operation, and today we have it,” he said. He added that outstanding issues between the government and the contractor were being resolved, stressing that the priority was to ensure the facility was put to good use for the benefit of Ghanaians.

items.title: FRSC confirms 20 dead in multiple crashes on Plateau route
items.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has confirmed the deaths of 20 people in a multiple road traffic crash along the Hawan Kibo-Jos route in Plateau. The Corps Public Education Officer (CPEO), Mr Osondu Ohaeri, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja. Ohaeri said the crash occurred at about 3:32 p.m. after Sopp Water Falls, with brake failure and loss of control identified as likely causes. He said 25 people were involved in the crash, comprising 23 males and two females. According to him, five people, comprising three males and two females, sustained injuries, while 20 males died in the crash. “Four vehicles were involved in the crash, including a Howo Sino truck with registration number AGL 525 YN. “Others were a Toyota Corolla with registration number AB 129 M and a Toyota Bummer bus operated by Yankari Express. “The fourth vehicle was a motorcycle whose registration particulars were not available. “The injured victims were evacuated to Ryom General Hospital and Vom Christian Hospital, while the deceased were deposited at JUTH Mortuary. “FRSC rescue personnel also cleared the obstruction caused by the crash and restored the affected highway section to traffic,” he said. Reacting to the incident, FRSC Corps Marshal, Malam Shehu Mohammed, expressed sadness over the loss of lives. He extended his condolences to the families, friends and associates of the deceased and prayed for the repose of their souls. Mohammed also wished the injured victims a speedy recovery and directed the crash investigation team to conduct a thorough investigation. He said the investigation should establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly the reported brake failure and loss of control. The Corps Marshal urged motorists, especially commercial and heavy-duty vehicle operators, to prioritise roadworthiness, maintenance, speed management and responsible driving. Mohammed further admonished drivers to exercise greater caution, stressing that the loss of 20 lives in one crash was not merely a statistic. “The loss of 20 lives in a single crash represents 20 families suddenly plunged into grief. Behind every number is a name, a home, a family and a future,” he said. Mohammed therefore urged all road users to take personal responsibility for safety, stressing that no journey was so urgent that it should end in death. (NAN) The post FRSC confirms 20 dead in multiple crashes on Plateau route appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Greater Accra teacher unions back nationwide strike over three key demands
items.description: The Greater Accra leadership of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) have backed the ongoing nationwide strike by pre-tertiary teachers. The unions are demanding urgent action from government on three key issues: placing promoted teachers on their new salary levels, concluding negotiations for a new Collective Agreement, and implementing the 20% Deprived Area Allowance. Addressing a press conference at the NAGRAT Hall in Nungua, Greater Accra Regional Chairman of NAGRAT, Henry Teitey Tetteh-Afi, said the concerns remain unresolved despite earlier government commitments. He said out of about 80,000 promoted teachers, only a little over 6,000 had so far been placed on their new salary levels. Mr Tettey-Afi said this was despite an agreement reached on August 31 between the unions and relevant government agencies to complete the placement process by the end of September. “We are here this morning to give our support to the national leadership in relation to the strike action that they declared exactly a week ago today,” he said. He said negotiations for a new Collective Agreement had also stalled, while the 20% allowance for teachers working in deprived and hard-to-reach areas had yet to be implemented. The regional leadership said it was not demanding that all outstanding issues be resolved immediately but wants the government to demonstrate concrete progress towards addressing them. “We want to see steps that are being taken that will ensure that these things are implemented within the shortest possible time,” Mr Tettey-Afi said. He added that the strike would continue until the government takes steps to address the concerns raised by the unions. The Greater Accra leadership has also appealed to parents to keep their children at home for as long as the strike remains in force.

items.title: Cancer du sein : le diagnostic moléculaire par la «MammaTyper », désormais disponible au Burkina Faso
items.description: Le diagnostic moléculaire par la MammaTyper est une technologie de dernière génération qui disponibilise les résultats en seulement six (06) heures.Le Burkina Faso devient le seul pays à en disposer dans la sous-région et même en Afrique. Finis donc les traitements coûteux ou inefficaces. Selon l’Observatoire mondial du cancer (Globocan), en 2024, Le Burkina Faso enregistrait 15 000 cas de cancer ont été avec 10 000 décès. La même année, un peu plus de 2 100 cas de cancer du sein ont été dépistés dans notre pays, avec 1 000 décès, soit environ trois décès de femmes par jour. Sous sa vision éclairée, le Camarade Président du Faso, Chef de l’Etat inscrit la lutte contre la maladie en une composante de l’Initiative présidentielle pour la santé (IPS). Ainsi, à travers l’Initiative présidentielle pour la santé (IPS), logée au Bureau national des grands projets du Burkina (BN-GPB), a permis de disponibiliser dans les Centres hospitaliers universitaires de Bogodogo (Ouagadougou) et de Pala (Bobo-Dioulasso) le diagnostic moléculaire du cancer du sein par la technique « MammaTyper ». « C’est pour nous, médecins soignants du Guiriko, une très belle initiative, qui permet au CHU de Pala d’être à un niveau optimal pour accompagner les femmes qui pourraient souffrir du cancer du sein », s’est réjoui la Pr Téné Marceline YAMEOGO, directrice des services médicaux et techniques. Dr Bruno ADJONBA, médecin biologiste au CHU de Pala, a, quant à lui, expliqué l’efficacité de MammaTyper : « En fonction du sous-type moléculaire, il propose un traitement adapté. Il n’y a plus vraiment à tâtonner sur ce qu’il faut administrer au patient », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également relevé qu’il s’agit de la première utilisation de cette technologie en Afrique. Il a ajouté que MammaTyper contribue non seulement à améliorer la prise en charge des patients, en offrant des résultats plus précis en seulement six heures. Dr Adjonba et d’autres médecins et techniciens ont effectué, à Hambourg en Allemagne, une immersion dans l’optique de maîtriser l’utilisation de la technologie MammaTyper. «Le sous-typage nécessitait anciennement un recours à l’extérieur », note, pour sa part, Dr Valentin KONSEGRE, médecin anatomo-biologiste au CHU de Pala. Cette technologie disponibiliée au Burkina permettra de réduire les évacuations sanitaires. Après l’installation du dispositif, le Coordonnateur national de l’IPS, Camarade Drissa Traoré, s’est rendu dans les deux CHU pour constater son fonctionnement. « Les tests sont faits avec beaucoup de précision. On a des résultats convaincants. On est sûr que la technologie est bien maîtrisée par nos praticiens », s’est-il réjoui. « Les résultats que nous avons obtenus ont été validés par la plateforme qui gère l’interprétation et le calcul des données », a renchéri Dr R. Alexie Ouédraogo, maître de conférences agrégé en histologie embryologisto-génétique au CHU de Bogodogo. Les prestations sont accessibles à l’ensemble des Burkinabè à des tarifs subventionnés. Le personnel de santé des CHU de Pala et de Bogodogo a témoigné sa reconnaissance au Camarade Président du Faso pour sa vision innovante et sa volonté, matérialisée par ces actions, d’œuvrer continuellement au bien-être des populations. À l’occasion de l’Octobre Rose 2026, le ministre de la Santé a encouragé les femmes à se faire dépister gratuitement du cancer du sein. DCRP / BN-GPB Minute.bf

items.title: Obasanjo, Jonathan, Gowon pay tribute to ex-Aso Villa chaplain William Okoye
items.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has described the late Rev. William Okoye as a statesman of faith and fearless voice of truth. Obasanjo stated this in a tribute read by Bishop Godwin Isaac at the Night of Tributes for Okoye, held at the National Christian Centre, Abuja, on Friday. Okoye, former General Overseer of All Christians Fellowship Mission (ACFM), was also a former Chaplain of the Aso Rock Villa Chapel. Obasanjo said Okoye’s death had created a monumental void across the nation, recalling their close working relationship between 1999 and 2007. He said Okoye, who served as his chaplain, provided wisdom and guidance during high-pressure situations, beyond his spiritual responsibilities. “As my chaplain, he was a steady, fearless, and uncompromising voice of truth,” Obasanjo said. He said Okoye understood that genuine gospel ministry must address the material realities confronting the people. Obasanjo recalled that Okoye served on the Presidential Advisory Council on Youth Affairs and represented the FCT at the National Political Reform Conference. He also served on the Christian Pilgrims Welfare Board and held leadership positions in the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN). Obasanjo said Okoye served as Chairman of CAN and PFN in Abuja, while also serving as CAN National Director on National Issues. Former President Goodluck Jonathan said he met Okoye while serving as Governor of Bayelsa State and worshipping at the Aso Rock Villa Chapel. Jonathan recalled that Okoye was then Deputy Chaplain to Rev. Obaje and later served as Chaplain during Jonathan’s presidency. He said Okoye eventually requested to leave the Villa Chapel and recommended Ven. Obioma Onwuzurumba as his successor, alongside Archbishop John Oyelade. “Nigeria will miss you. Your family will miss you. The church will miss you. You stood for integrity,” Jonathan said. Former Head of State, Gen. Yakubu Gowon, described Okoye as a pioneer of Nigeria Prays and praised his leadership, integrity, humility and commitment. Gowon, who was unable to attend physically because of a trip to the United Kingdom, delivered his tribute virtually. He said Okoye’s memory would remain evergreen, recalling his support for the Nigeria Prays movement since its inception in 1996. Sen. Victor Umeh, who represented Mr Peter Obi, described Okoye as a brother from the same local government area in Anambra State. Umeh said Okoye prayed for peace during Anambra’s political crisis and worked to promote stability in the state. Pastor Mrs Toyin Okoye, wife of the deceased, thanked God for her husband’s life, describing him affectionately as “Mine”. She said Okoye told doctors at the hospital that he was not afraid of death and appreciated those who prayed for and visited them. She particularly acknowledged Pastor Enoch Adeboye and other Christian leaders who supported the family during the period. “Your life of integrity touched lives, including my own life. “You have fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith,” she said. Dr Paul Enenche, founder of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, said Okoye was passionate about Nigeria’s spiritual and physical wellbeing. Enenche said Okoye believed God would raise Christians who would contribute significantly to the transformation of Nigeria. The President of CAN, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, described Okoye as a preacher, trainer and mentor who dedicated his life to God and humanity. Okoh quoted Psalm 116:15 and John 11:25, saying Christians did not mourn as those without hope. NAN reports that Okoye, who served as Chaplain to two Nigerian presidents, will be buried next week in his hometown in Anambra. (NAN) The post Obasanjo, Jonathan, Gowon pay tribute to ex-Aso Villa chaplain William Okoye appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul’s apology demand
items.description: North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul’s military said Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North. Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue. Early Saturday, “our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea,” Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan. “South Korea, the US, and Japan are maintaining a robust defense posture through close information sharing regarding North Korean ballistic missiles,” it said, adding the missile flew more than 700 kilometres (435 miles). Seoul and the US-led United Nations Command found that last month’s explosion inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice, was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South side of the border. North Korea’s military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off following leader Kim Jong Un’s designation of South Korea as his country’s “principal enemy” in 2024. The mines responsible for the blast, which left three soldiers wounded, were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defence minister Kang Shin-chul. South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier. Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, responded by calling Seoul “really despicable” on Friday and once again denied Pyongyang was behind the blasts. She ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch” and said the military’s demand her country apologise was “quite ridiculous.” Kim also warned Pyongyang was “ready for anything” Seoul might do over the mine blast — remarks followed the next morning by North Korea’s ballistic missile launch. – ‘Escalating’ tensions – Analysts said the launch would be viewed as a show of force in response to the South Korean government’s diplomatic efforts, effectively rejecting engagement. “Seoul called for easing tensions, but Pyongyang answered by escalating them,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP. “The message is that the North is pursuing… confrontation in response to goodwill,” he added. South Korea’s defence minister said on Tuesday the military had “a range of necessary measures at our disposal, and we will implement them in stages” to respond to the DMZ incident, without providing further detail. The South’s Unification Minister, Chung Dong-young, also proposed talks to address issues along the border to Pyongyang on Friday. Kim Yo Jong, however, dismissed Chung’s suggestion of talks as a “wild dream and unilateral jargon.” The flare-up comes at a sensitive time when US President Donald Trump’s recent overtures to Pyongyang have raised concerns that Seoul — an ally of Washington — could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North. South Korea’s opposition People Power Party on Friday accused Lee of failing to criticise Pyongyang when warranted even as he takes a hard line on Ukraine for publicly disclosing the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war, an arrangement Seoul believed should be confidential. “South Korean soldiers have been injured, and far from receiving an apology, we have been mocked by North Korea,” the opposition party said in a statement. “We fail to see how selectively turning a blind eye to North Korea serves South Korea’s dignity or the safety of its people.” AFP The post North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul’s apology demand appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: États-Unis | L’état-major privé de la guerre «superintelligente»
items.description: La décision du secrétaire à la Défense américain Pete Hegseth de confier la conception de la guerre de demain à des figures civiles du capitalisme algorithmique marque un tournant historique dans la gestion de la violence d’État. Mahjoub Lotfi Belhedi * À travers le Projet Meridian et la création d’un Commandement de la guerre autonome (Autowarcom), l’administration américaine ne cherche plus simplement à moderniser ses armées : elle acte le passage de la simple intelligence artificielle à ce que Donald Trump, qui affectionne les superlatifs, formalise désormais par décret sous l’appellation de «superintelligence» . Ce glissement sémantique et politique valide une course aux armements où la supériorité militaire absolue exige une force de calcul supérieure, affranchie des limites cognitives humaines. Un duopole technologique au service de la guerre Dans cette reconfiguration, les rôles sont soigneusement distribués pour capitaliser sur l’expérience directe des conflits contemporains. Elon Musk, fort de l’infrastructure globale de Starlink et des capacités génératives de xAI, est mandaté pour identifier et structurer les technologies de rupture indispensables aux futurs conflits. Son implication s’enracine dans la réalité des guerres actuelles, où la constellation Starlink est devenue la colonne vertébrale indispensable des communications militaires et du ciblage en temps réel sur les fronts les plus critiques, à l’instar de l’Ukraine où il a déjà fait ses preuves. À ses côtés, Palmer Luckey, fondateur d’Anduril Industries, apporte l’expertise opérationnelle d’une start-up militaire nativement conçue pour la guerre automatisée. Loin de la théorie, les systèmes d’Anduril sont déjà activement déployés sur les théâtres d'opérations modernes : ses drones intercepteurs autonomes, ses missiles à longue portée comme le Barracuda-500M, ainsi que sa participation au programme Titan – un système mobile de renseignement par IA qui fusionne les données de multiples capteurs pour accélérer l'identification des cibles – redéfinissent déjà la vitesse d’exécution des frappes. Un conflit d’intérêts systémique Ensemble, les deux technologues transforment le Pentagone en incubateur, où la planification stratégique de la nation s’aligne directement sur les intérêts de firmes privées. Cette hybridation institutionnalise un conflit d’intérêts systémique, transformant ces deux entrepreneurs en juges et parties de la défense nationale. En laissant des industriels rédiger eux-mêmes la doctrine de la superintelligence militaire, l’État abdique sa fonction de régulateur neutre pour devenir le client captif d’un duopole technologique. Dès lors, la dynamique des conflits mondiaux n’obéira plus seulement aux équilibres diplomatiques traditionnels, elle sera dictée par le rythme d’optimisation des algorithmes de combat et par l’obligation, pour ces multinationales, de valider la puissance de leur modèle sur des théâtres d’opérations en constante extension. Confrontée à cette course effrénée où la décision ultime est transférée à des entités computationnelles qui dépassent notre entendement, une question fondamentale demeure : en abdiquant notre propre discernement face à cette superintelligence pour l’armer et la rendre souveraine, n’avons-nous pas initié un mécanisme d’escalade irréversible où l’humanité, devenue obsolète sur le champ de bataille, ne sera plus que le spectateur impuissant et la victime collatérale de sa propre destitution ? * Stratège en réflexion IA. items.title: UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'
items.description: The UAE’s attorney general said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel had planned a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, the official UAE news agency WAM reported Saturday. The news agency quoted Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying that according to the initial findings of an investigation, “the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and had “attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft”. Barred from flying The co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a flydubai flight to Israel had previously been barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his extremist views, multiple media outlets reported. Scrutiny into the alleged assailant — who was identified in the reports as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami — and his motives has intensified after Wednesday’s drama aboard a Dubai-Tel Aviv route that officials say narrowly avoided catastrophe. During the flydubai flight, the jet’s Indian captain was assaulted by his co-pilot but he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that Omani authorities had banned the pilot from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views, citing people familiar with the matter. CNN , citing two sources familiar with the matter, reported the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about extremist views. Al Arabiya , citing an informed source, reported that Omani authorities determined that the co-pilot held extremist views. The broadcaster said he had also spent time in Syria, raising concerns he may have been influenced by radical groups there. ABC News , citing senior intelligence and law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation, reported the suspect had allegedly been found in possession of extremist materials while he was a trainee.

items.title: Burkina : Le GAGF et Média’Vert plaident pour un cadre réglementaire de la RNA
items.description: Le Groupe d’Action pour la Gestion Forestière (GAGF), en collaboration avec Média’ vert, a tenu le vendredi 02 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une rencontre d’échange consacrée à la Régénération Naturelle Assistée (RNA). Cette rencontre qui visait à présenter les avantages de cette pratique, s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un plaidoyer pour l’adoption d’un texte réglementaire sur la RNA au Burkina Faso. La RNA est une technique agro-forestière qui consiste à protéger et entretenir des espèces ligneuses poussant naturellement, ou des rejets de souches dans un champ ou dans des espaces sylvopastoraux. Il s'agit de sélectionner les sujets et de les épargner au cours du défrichement en saison sèche, du labour et des différentes opérations d'entretien du champ en saison des pluies. Cette approche présente selon le modérateur Sidnoma Issaka Kaboré, des avantages tant sur les plans environnemental, agricole que social. Modérateur du GAGF, Sidnoma Issaka Kaboré Selon une étude sur la régénération du karité conduite dans certains pays de la sous-région dont le Burkina Faso, sur sept techniques de régénération des plants couramment pratiquées, la RNA est la plus efficace. Le taux de réussite de cette méthode varie entre 77,78% et 78,89% en fonction de la zone phytogéographique contre 55,56% pour la plantation, 25,33% pour le semis direct dans des buissons, 15,33% pour la transplantation de sauvageons. Des études du CIFOR-ICRAF quant à elles montrent que cette pratique améliore significativement la fertilité des sols et les rendements agricoles, avec des hausses allant de 15 à 30 %. Elle permet également d’accroître les revenus des producteurs. Au vu des avantages de la RNA, l’adoption d’un texte réglementaire permettrait, selon Issaka Kaboré, aux différents acteurs de travailler dans un cadre harmonisé et conformément aux normes de l’État. « Ce sera également l’occasion d’encourager les différents acteurs sur le terrain à s’investir pleinement afin que la RNA puisse se renforcer et contribuer à la reforestation.» a-t-il indiqué. À en croire le modérateur Sidnoma Kaboré, un certain nombre de concertations avec les services techniques, des producteurs, des collectivités ainsi qu’avec différents ministères, ont déjà été effectuées dans le cadre du plaidoyer pour l’adoption dudit texte réglementaire sur la pratique de la RNA au Burkina Faso. « Il y a également eu des formations, notamment sur le plaidoyer et sur la RNA, ainsi qu’un ensemble d’activités visant à informer davantage les acteurs sur cette initiative et à les amener à intégrer la RNA dans leurs démarches et leurs activités. » a-t-il souligné. Le Groupe d’Action pour la Gestion Forestière (GAGF), en collaboration avec Média’Vert, entend par ailleurs faire en sorte que les initiatives qui seront prises après le plaidoyer puissent être effectivement mises en pratique sur le terrain. L'objectif du plaidoyer, selon les organisateurs, est de faire adopter un texte réglementaire arrêté ou décret sur la RNA au Burkina Faso par le décideur principal, à savoir le Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'eau, des ressources animales et halieutiques, au cours de l'année 2026 ou pour les premiers mois de 2027. Il s'agit spécifiquement, dans ce décret ou cet arrêté, de définir la RNA en tenant compte de la nature des écosystèmes dans lesquels elle est pratiquée, ainsi que des autres formes de régénération des plants qui peuvent la renforcer. Photo de famille Il s'agit aussi de définir une tenure spécifique aux arbres résultant de la pratique de la RNA qui soit incitative pour les producteurs, et d'arrêter un protocole technique pour la conduite de la RNA. Enfin, il s'agit engager les services techniques déconcentrés dans la diffusion et le suivi du respect de ce protocole, et d' engager la responsabilité des collectivités territoriales sur la prise en compte de la RNA dans les documents de planification. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO Minute.bf

Siavash Jamshidi was accused of targeting security personnel during mass demonstrations that peaked in January in which thousands of people were killed. Since that time, Iranian authorities have stepped up executions of convicts linked to the unrest. “Jamshidi was sentenced to death on charges of moharebeh through brandishing and firing a firearm, as well as conspiracy and collusion against national security,” Iran’s judiciary said, using the legal term moharebeh to mean “waging war against God”. The judiciary’s Mizan Online website said he was also found guilty of offences not related to the protests, including “fraud, making threats, theft, possession and carrying of an illegal military-grade weapon”. Other charges included “complicity in kidnapping, brandishing a weapon to intimidate, and intentional infliction of bodily harm”. Mizan said Jamshidi was “active” during the demonstrations, which were sparked in December last year by grievances over living costs in Iran, but peaked on January 8 and 9 with huge rallies. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths in the unrest, attributing the violence to “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. Foreign-based NGOs however maintain that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. US President Donald Trump threatened at the time to intervene militarily in Iran. Weeks later in late February, the United States and Israel launched a joint attack on the Islamic republic, triggering the Middle East war. Since then, arrests and executions have multiplied in Iran, linked both to the war and the protests. In 2025, Iran executed at least 1,639 people, the largest number in any year since 1989, according to the NGOs Iran Human Rights and Together Against the Death Penalty. Amnesty International says Iran carries out more executions than any country except China. AFP The post Iran executes man linked to anti-government protests appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Galerie Grafiflow | Hammadi Ben Saad ou la liberté du geste
items.description: La galerie Grafiflow (43, rue du Commandant Béjaoui, la Soukra), au nord de Tunis, propose une exposition du peintre Hammadi Ben Saad, décédé le 25 juillet 2025 à l’âge de 77 ans. Joliment intitulée ‘‘Remember Me’’, comme pour interpeller ceux qui ont côtoyé l’homme et apprécié son œuvre, pour qu’ils ne l’oublient pas et continuent de les faire vivre parmi eux, l’exposition se tiendra du 9 octobre au 1 er novembre 2026. Nous reproduisons ci-dessous le texte de présentation de l’exposition réalisé par la directrice artistique de l’exposition. Rim Ben Boubaker * Cette exposition propose un regard rétrospectif sur plus de cinquante ans de création de Hammadi Ben Saad, figure singulière de la scène artistique tunisienne **. Des premières figures aux recherches autour du trait, du papier, de la matière et de l’accident, jusqu’aux visages, aux masques, aux hommes des cavernes et aux monochromes abstraits, elle retrace les transformations d’un langage artistique toujours en mouvement. L’exposition met en lumière une œuvre construite dans la liberté du geste, l’expérimentation et une relation instinctive à la matière. À travers une sélection d’œuvres, d’archives et de documents, le parcours fait dialoguer différentes périodes sans les enfermer dans une chronologie stricte. Présentée après sa disparition en 2025, l’exposition porte également une dimension particulière : celle de poursuivre le dialogue avec une œuvre qui continue de vivre au-delà de son créateur. Une œuvre en mouvement Faut-il encore présenter Hammadi Ben Saad ? Autodidacte, Hammadi Ben Saad a développé, depuis le début des années 1960, une œuvre profondément singulière, construite au fil de plusieurs décennies de mutations, de déplacements et de transformations. Son parcours ne se laisse pas enfermer dans une seule manière de peindre. Cette exposition est née du désir d’appréhender son œuvre dans son ensemble. Elle ne cherche pas à reconstruire une chronologie figée, mais à suivre un mouvement : celui d’un artiste qui n’a cessé de déplacer son regard, d’explorer de nouvelles voies et de remettre son langage en jeu. Des premières figures des années 1970 aux recherches autour du trait et de la ligne, des compositions nourries par l’accident, les images imprimées et la matière aux visages, masques et figures humaines, figures hybrides ou «hommes des cavernes» , comme il aimait les nommer, jusqu’aux monochromes abstraits et aux travaux des dernières années, l’exposition fait apparaître les différentes étapes d’un cheminement sans cesse en mouvement. Elle permet ainsi de revenir sur ce parcours, mais aussi de faire surgir des correspondances entre des œuvres et des périodes parfois éloignées. Peintures, archives et documents sont réunis pour donner à voir élaboration progressive de son langage artistique. Présenter Hammadi aujourd’hui, après sa disparition, prend nécessairement une autre dimension. Il ne s’agit pas de clore le parcours de l’artiste au moment où sa vie s’est arrêtée. Au contraire, son absence offre un autre temps, une autre dimension à son œuvre : ceux de la découverte, de la relecture et de la rencontre avec de nouveaux regards. Ou peut-être une manière de poursuivre la conversation avec lui. Si Hammadi n’est plus là, son œuvre n’est pas statique. Elle continue de circuler, de susciter des questions, de faire surgir de nouvelles correspondances et de rencontrer d’autres regards. C’est dans cet espace que cette exposition souhaite se tenir : non pas comme la conclusion d’une histoire, mais comme une invitation à la poursuivre. Car le plus bel hommage que l’on puisse rendre à un artiste n’est pas seulement de raconter son histoire. C’est de pousser la porte de son univers, de prendre le temps de regarder, de se laisser surprendre et, peut-être, de se laisser toucher. * Curatrice. ** Voilà ce que l'auteure, Rym Ben Boubaker, écrivait le 26 juillet 2026 sur sa page Facebook en apprenant le décès, la veille, de cet artiste hors normes de tous points de vue : «C’est avec une immense tristesse que j’écris ces mots en hommage à Hammadi Ben Saad, un artiste rare, un homme vrai, un être d’une humanité profonde. J’ai eu le privilège de croiser sa route, de partager avec lui des moments de création, de réflexion, de complicité. Travailler à ses côtés fut un honneur, parler de son art, une richesse. Il m’a accueillie avec tant de générosité, tant d’amour… Il m’aimait comme sa fille, et ce lien restera à jamais précieux dans mon cœur. Hammadi n’était pas seulement un artiste : il était un souffle, une lumière, un regard tendre sur le monde. Sa voix, son œuvre, son engagement laissent un vide immense dans la scène artistique, mais surtout dans la vie de ceux qui l’ont connu et aimé. Il s’en va, mais il laisse derrière lui une traînée d’étoiles, des couleurs, des mots et des silences pleins de sens. Et dans ce silence désormais, son art continue de parler… Son absence résonne, mais sa présence demeure. Dans chaque regard ému face à une de ses œuvres, Il est là. Toujours là. Repose en paix Si Hammadi.» L’article Galerie Grafiflow | Hammadi Ben Saad ou la liberté du geste est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: India-Pakistan blockbuster brings cricket fever to Japan baseball field
items.description: One of sport’s fiercest rivalries descended on a sleepy corner of Japan on Saturday as India and Pakistan clashed in the men’s cricket final at the Asian Games on a converted baseball field. The neighbours only meet in international tournaments because of long-running political tensions and matches between them typically attract television audiences of hundreds of millions back home. The gold-medal encounter in a suburban park in Nagoya was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for Indians and Pakistanis living in Japan. They lined up hours before the game to get into the cosy 2,500-capacity purpose-built Korogi Athletic Park Stadium. Pakistan’s Saim Ayub (L) celebrates as India’s Vaibhav Sooryavanshiis is caught out during the men’s cricket final match between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. — AFP “I think this is never going to happen again, India against Pakistan in Japan,” long-time Nagoya resident Umer Dar, draped in a Pakistan flag, told AFP . “I’m crazy about cricket but I never have the opportunity to watch it live because I’ve lived here for 26 years.” The last time India and Pakistan collided was at the T20 World Cup in February, where they played in front of a sell-out 35,000 crowd in Sri Lanka. The Asian Games setting was significantly more modest, with trees and a baseball pitcher’s mound just beyond the boundary. The atmosphere was as passionate as ever though, with fans waving flags and cheering every ball from the temporary stands. “We bought tickets three months back when they started selling them,” said Tokyo resident and India supporter Mohammed Kashim Raja. India’s Ishan Kishan (L) sweeps the ball during the men’s cricket final match between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. — AFP “At the time it was easy but it became really difficult for others to get them. “We heard that many people were selling them for high prices.” Cricket is a niche sport in Japan and neutrals at the final appeared to be virtually non-existent. ‘Always crazy’ There was more of a casual crowd at the bronze-medal match between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh earlier, on a warm and sunny day. Teachers Hiromi Niwa and Miki Kaede, both from nearby Gifu, said they knew nothing about cricket and had bought tickets out of curiosity. After reading a free leaflet explaining the rules and watching some of the action, Kaede said it had been a “really fun” experience. She was disappointed that their tickets did not get them into the final. “We didn’t realise that India against Pakistan was such a big deal until we actually searched for it,” she said. Pakistan players celebrate the dismissal of India’s Shreyas Iyer during the men’s cricket final match between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. — AFP Cricket has a growing presence in Japan and the sport got a huge boost when India played their first-ever T20 international against Japan last week. The historic match, celebrating 75 years of diplomatic relations, took place at Japan’s modest Sano International Cricket Ground outside Tokyo. It was Japan’s first T20 game against a full-member nation, and they gave India a huge fright before losing by two runs in a rain-shortened match. Kushal Gowda, an Indian fan living in Tokyo, said Japanese people were “trying to understand” cricket. “We were trying to explain to our colleagues in our office and they were curious and keen to know what it was about,” he said. Indian fans arrive for the men’s cricket final between Pakistan and India during the 2026 Asian Games at the Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin on October 3, 2026. — AFP “They kind of compared it with baseball.” The crowd for the Asian Games final was overwhelmingly supporting India, with only a few Pakistan flags and shirts dotted around the ground. A cheer went up when the gates opened to let fans in, and the party continued when the game began under clear skies. “Even if it’s in Japan, the craze of India versus Pakistan is always there,” said Tokyo-based India fan Afroz Khan. “Anywhere they play in the world, it’s always crazy.”

items.title: Envoi d’avions au Niger, FMI, réserves de change, pouvoir d’achat : Tebboune s’exprime
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, s’exprime sur plusieurs sujets d’actualité nationale et internationale. Dans une nouvelle entrevue avec la presse nationale, il s’exprime sur les raisons de l’envoi d’avions militaires au Niger et lance à l’occasion un message fort à l’égard de ceux qui cherchent à déstabiliser ce pays et à provoquer l’Algérie. Baisse des réserves de change : Tebboune contredit le FMI Il évoque les questions relatives au pouvoir d’achat et la hausse des prix des fruits et légumes, et aborde les dernières prévisions du FMI sur la baisse des réserves de change de l’Algérie. L’entrevue sera diffusée ce samedi sur la Télévision algérienne. Sur le pouvoir d’achat, le président Tebboune a épargné les « agricultures qui ne sont pas à l’origine de la hausse des prix ». « La majorité des agriculteurs n’est pas responsable de la hausse des prix (…) Nous devons sauvegarder le pouvoir d’achat des citoyens. Il y a des responsables locaux que j’ai limogé », a-t-il tranché. Coupe d’État au Niger : Tebboune explique pourquoi il a envoyé des avions militaires Sur les prévisions du FMI concernant une baisse drastique des réserves de change du pays à 29 milliards de dollars à l’horizon 2031, le président Tebboune a assuré qu’elles seront plus élevées. « Nous travaillons pour augmenter nos revenus hors hydrocarbures. Ce n’est pas une question de devises. C’est une question de souveraineté », a-t-il dit. Sur l’escale effectuée par le président iranien à l’aéroport d’Alger, le président Tebboune a répondu : « Un président qui demande de se poser dans un aéroport algérien, il est le bienvenu ». Le chef de l’État a ajouté : « Nous ne renonçons pas à notre relation avec la Russie, ni avec la Chine, ni les États-Unis », a-t-il dit. Sur la décision d’envoyer des avions militaires au Niger, le président Tebboune a répondu aussi : « Le premier ministre nigérien était en Algérie. Dans le même temps, il y a une tentative de coup d’État au Niger. Qu’est-ce cela signifie ? Une provocation à l’égard de l’Algérie ? Moi aussi, je vais envoyer des avions ». L’article Envoi d’avions au Niger, FMI, réserves de change, pouvoir d’achat : Tebboune s’exprime est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Indus Waters Treaty abeyance puts millions at risk, UNHRC event warns
items.description: UNITED NATIONS: India’s decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance has raised concerns over the water security, agriculture and livelihoods of millions of people dependent on the Indus Basin, as the six-decade-old agreement faces one of its most serious challenges. The concerns were discussed on Friday, Oct 2, at a side event held in Geneva on the margins of the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council. The Council’s current session is being held from Sept 7 to Oct 7. The event, titled “Water Justice and Climate Resilience: Advancing Transboundary Cooperation in South Asia and the Middle East,” brought together legal experts, researchers, diplomats, practitioners and civil society representatives to discuss international water law, human rights, climate resilience, environmental justice and management of shared rivers. “Trans-boundary Water Challenges in South Asia” was among the principal themes, with particular attention to the Indus River system and the legal and institutional framework governing shared waters. The Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA), which administers the proceedings over the IWT, has determined that the treaty remains in force despite India’s decision to place it in abeyance. India has rejected the arbitration process, while Pakistan has cited the court’s order as supporting its position that the agreement remains effective. Rashida Abbas, founder of the Hydro-Justice Student Research & Policy Fellowship and a PhD candidate at the University of Geneva, addressed the South Asian dimension of the discussion, focusing particularly on the Indus system. Abbas said rivers should not be viewed solely as matters between states because their consequences are experienced directly by people and communities. “Rivers are not experienced only by states,” Abbas said. “They are experienced by people.” She linked water governance with human rights, noting that decisions concerning rivers can affect drinking water, agriculture, livelihoods, communities and health. Abbas argued that the future management of South Asia’s shared waters should be based on law, dialogue, science, functioning institutions and justice. She also stressed that trans-boundary agreements should not become optional when relations between states deteriorate. The discussion addressed concerns about using shared water resources as instruments of political pressure. Abbas highlighted the interests of downstream communities and the need for legal frameworks to protect their water security and human rights. Other speakers placed the Indus dispute within a broader discussion of trans-boundary water challenges. Majid Hawi Alwan addressed geopolitical pressures surrounding shared water systems in arid regions, including the Gulf and wider Middle East. His contribution focused on regional approaches in which water security is treated as a shared necessity rather than an instrument of unilateral leverage. Seraina Eldada brought a mediation and diplomacy perspective, examining the institutional design of transboundary water arrangements and the role of third-party mediation and permanent mechanisms in resolving disputes. Harmayn Mujahid, a legal scholar and fellowship coordination officer, linked water insecurity with human rights concerns. The discussion considered how changing river patterns and climate-related stress can affect vulnerable communities and why questions of equity need to be considered alongside state sovereignty in international water law. Tahir Mahmood addressed the relationship between resource scarcity and security, including risks associated with water-related tensions in regions already affected by political and territorial disputes. He also discussed prevention and resilience in the context of what he described as “hydro-terrorism.” The contributors noted that shared river systems face increasing pressure from climate change, population growth, environmental degradation and rising demand for freshwater. For Pakistan, the Indus Basin is particularly significant because its waters support agriculture, food production and millions of livelihoods. The river system has sustained human settlements in the region for thousands of years. The Geneva discussion placed the current India-Pakistan dispute within a wider question of whether institutions governing shared rivers can continue to function during periods of political tension. The PCA award represents a significant development in the legal proceedings, but it has not resolved the underlying political disagreement between India and Pakistan. The award and the separate order concerning interim measures, however, remain on the PCA’s official record. The Geneva meeting underscored the importance of maintaining established mechanisms for dialogue and dispute resolution as countries sharing vital water resources confront both political tensions and growing environmental pressures.

items.title: Greece: Rights Defenders on Trial
items.description: Click to expand Image Left: Panayote Dimitras. Right: Tommy Olsen. © 2019 EIN Secretariat – Agnes Ciccarone © 2015 Adam Rosser (Athens, October 3, 2026) – The ongoing prosecution of two prominent human rights defenders in Greece is a politically-motivated attempt to silence their efforts to expose abuses against migrants, Human Rights Watch said today. The trial of the two activists, Panayote Dimitras and Tommy Olsen, is set to begin on the Greek island of Rhodes on October 6, 2026. “The upcoming trial of Panayote Dimitras and Tommy Olsen is a blatant attempt to criminalize and silence their legitimate human rights work,” said Eva Cossé, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Prosecutors should drop this politically motivated case against Dimitras and Olsen once and for all.” Dimitras, founder and president of the Greek nongovernmental group Greek Helsinki Monitor, and Olsen, a Norwegian national and founder of the nongovernmental group Aegean Boat Report, are being prosecuted alongside two Cameroonian asylum seekers on charges of “forming or joining for profit and by profession a criminal organization with the purpose of facilitating the entry and stay of third country nationals into Greek territory.” If convicted, they face up to 20 years in prison. The charges brought against the activists in early 2023 stem from their peaceful human rights and humanitarian work, Human Rights Watch said. The indictment seeks to criminalize the defendants’ practice of notifying Greek authorities and international bodies of the whereabouts of newly arrived asylum seekers and migrants on the Greek islands, to help ensure that they have access to the country’s asylum procedure and not be pushed back to Türkiye. Dimitras and Olsen have for years documented and exposed human rights violations against asylum seekers and migrants, including violent pushbacks by Greek authorities, that have been characterized as “systematic” by the European Court of Human Rights. On May 15, a Norwegian appeals court rejected Greek authorities’ request to extradite Olsen, who lives in Norway, to Greece through a European Arrest Warrant. The Norwegian court concluded that the acts described by Greek authorities do not constitute criminal offenses under Norwegian law, noting that assisting someone in initiating an asylum procedure is a lawful act protected by international treaties. The court also found that extraditing Olsen to Greece would present a real risk of violating his right to freedom of expression. Because Greek prosecutors have maintained arrest warrants, including the European Arrest Warrant, against Olsen, Olsen faces arrest and detention if he travels to Greece to defend himself. Dimitras who lives in Greece, is not in detention but is subject to a travel ban preventing him from leaving the country. The court summons specifies that, under Greek law, defendants will be tried in their absence if they do not appear or are not represented by a lawyer. Proceeding on that basis would amount to an in absentia prosecution under international law. Under international law, including the European Convention on Human Rights, to which Greece is a party, anyone convicted in absentia, who later returns to the country where the conviction was issued, should have the opportunity to a fresh determination of the merits of their case by a court there. The prosecution of Dimitras and Olsen is part of a wider, well-documented pattern of Greek authorities misusing criminal and administrative law to harass and intimidate human rights activists and civil society organizations defending the rights of asylum seekers and migrants. In January, a Greek court on the island of Lesbos acquitted 24 humanitarian workers of similar charges, after prosecutors subjected them to a devastating seven-year legal ordeal. Despite this high-profile acquittal, Greek authorities have failed to change course, Human Rights Watch said. In February, the Greek government passed a migration law that makes membership in a nongovernmental organization an aggravating circumstance in migration-related criminal offenses, in some cases elevating them to felonies, with draconian penalties. In 2023, the then-United Nations special rapporteur on the situation of human rights defenders, Mary Lawlor, stated in a report to the UN Human Rights Council that “human rights lawyers, humanitarian workers, volunteers and journalists [working on migration in Greece] have been subjected to smear campaigns, a changing regulatory environment, threats and attacks, and the misuse of criminal law against them, to a shocking degree.” Lawlor has also said that the criminal investigation against Dimitras and Olsen “strongly appears” to be arbitrary. “The Norwegian court firmly recognized that helping people present themselves to seek asylum is not a crime,” Cossé said. “Greek authorities should take a cue from the court and end this farce by dropping the case and halting the weaponization of criminal law against human rights defenders.”

Car crashes into crowd in Australia, 10 injured
items.description: A driver lost control and crashed his car into a crowd of rugby league fans in the eastern Australian city of Newcastle on Saturday, injuring 10 people including children, police said. Thousands of supporters had gathered to farewell local rugby league side the Newcastle Knights ahead of their grand final match against the Sydney Roosters on Sunday. But the festive environment was shattered when an 18-year-old rugby fan “driving erratically” lost control of his vehicle and crashed into the crowd, police said. “He was revving the car, he was excited, he was a supporter, he was there for the joy of the moment,” Newcastle Mayor Gavin Morris told national broadcaster ABC. “Somehow he lost control of the car… and he’s gone into the crowd.” Two people were in a critical condition — a five-year-old girl and 67-year-old man. Two other young children were hurt, police said. The driver had been taken into custody. “One person made a decision in a split second that put everyone at risk,” said Jenny Aitchison, the roads minister for the state of New South Wales. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said “my thoughts are with everyone injured or involved in the horrible incident this morning in Newcastle”. “Rugby league brings people together, and this should have been a weekend of excitement and pride for Newcastle fans,” he wrote in a post on X. And Knights captain Kalyn Ponga said on Instagram: “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community.” “Sending our love and support.”

items.title: Rizwan, NCCIA tight-lipped after player appears for questioning
items.description: LAHORE: Pakistan’s wicket-keeper/batter Mohammad Rizwan appeared before the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) here on Friday in a case concerning allegations of online betting, gambling and leaking of team information from the dressing room during the Test series in England earlier this year. Neither Rizwan nor any NCCIA official were ready to respond to media queries after the cricketer came out of the agency’s office after more than three and a half hours of investigation conducted by four NCCIA officials. Rizwan, 34, was served a notice by the NCCIA under the Criminal Procedure Code Section 160. When asked how the conduct of the agency’s official was and what questions he faced, a smiling Rizwan said: “I am deaf (in this connection), the conduct (of NCCIA officials) was good. I am feeling hungry; so let me go” before leaving the venue. It may be mentioned here that the NCCIA had confiscated Rizwan’s mobile phone in England on Aug 30, reportedly, having some secret information. The agency had promised that it will return the phone in three hours but it was not given to the player before he was summoned for inquiry on Friday. It is still not clear if the NCCIA has returned Rizwan’s phone. And there is no information if the agency will again summon the player. It is learnt Rizwan was summoned for his face recognition, which is necessary for daily forensics of the phone. Published in Dawn, October 3rd, 2026

items.title: Économie russe : sous pression budgétaire, les régions réduisent les indemnités versées aux familles des soldats morts en Ukraine
items.description: Mardi 29 septembre, le gouvernement de la région de Saratov, située sur la Volga, à la frontière avec le Kazakhstan, a publié un décret divisant par dix l'indemnité régionale versée aux familles des soldats tués au combat en Ukraine. Celle-ci passera d'un million de roubles (environ 10 600 euros) à 100 000 roubles (environ 1 060 euros) à partir du 1er novembre В Саратовской области в 10 раз сократили выплату членам семей погибших участников войны в Украине », Радио Свобода , 1er octobre 2026.'> 1 . Ces derniers mois, plusieurs régions russes ont réduit, voire supprimé, cette indemnité, restée jusque-là stable depuis le lancement de l'invasion en 2022. Depuis l'automne 2025, la république du Bachkortostan a réduit à trois reprises cette indemnité, qui est passée de deux millions de roubles (environ 21 200 euros) à 100 000 roubles (environ 1 060 euros). Les autorités des oblasts de Kirov et d'Omsk ont quant à elles divisé par deux son montant, qui est passé d'un million de roubles à 500 000 roubles au début de l’année, soit environ 5 300 euros. Dans l'oblast d'Irkoutsk, l'Assemblée législative régionale a finalement retiré le 20 mai une disposition, adoptée en première lecture, qui visait à diviser par deux le montant de l'indemnité Законопроект о повышенной выплате участникам СВО приняло Законодательное собрание Иркутской области », TK Gorod , 20 mai 2026.'> 2 . Selon l’économiste Janis Kluge, ces baisses sont remarquables car le montant des indemnités était resté stable depuis le lancement de l’invasion, en février 2022 Russian recruitment roundup, September 2026 », Russianomics , 10 septembre 2026.'> 3 . De plus, contrairement aux primes d’engagement, qui jouent un rôle direct pour inciter les hommes russes à signer un contrat avec l’armée, les indemnités versées en cas de blessure ou de décès ne constituent pas un engagement de vente. Comme l’explique Kluge : « Personne ne souhaite penser à sa propre mort lorsqu’il signe un contrat ». Ces baisses s’inscrivent dans un contexte de détérioration de la situation budgétaire russe au niveau des régions. Selon la Cour des comptes russe, 56 régions ont enregistré des déficits budgétaires au premier trimestre (contre 46 l’an dernier), et 74 régions (sur 85) ont fini l’année 2025 avec un déficit, selon l’agence de notation ACRA. Sberbank anticipe un déficit budgétaire cumulé des régions de 2 000 milliards de roubles cette année Сбербанк спрогнозировал рекордную « дыру » в бюджетах регионов на 2 триллиона рублей », The Moscow Times , 2 septembre 2026.'> 4 . En 2021, avant l'invasion de l'Ukraine, les régions russes avaient enregistré un excédent d'environ 400 milliards de roubles. Les indemnités régionales sont toutes largement inférieures aux sommes versées aux familles par l'État fédéral, qui dépassent 10 millions de roubles (environ 100 000 euros) par soldat tué. Pour le Kremlin, les familles des soldats tués en Ukraine ainsi que les vétérans représentent un enjeu politique de plus en plus important, alors que le bilan humain ne cesse de s'alourdir. Selon l'état-major ukrainien, l'armée russe aurait subi plus de 1,5 million de pertes, tués et blessés confondus, depuis février 2022. Les élections législatives de septembre ont vu l'élection à la Douma de 46 vétérans de la guerre en Ukraine, selon la présidente de la commission électorale centrale, Ella Pamfilova, soit un peu plus de 10 % de la chambre. En 2024, Poutine a lancé un nouveau programme, baptisé « Le Temps des héros » (« Время героев »), visant à préparer des vétérans à occuper de hautes fonctions dans l'administration. Trois personnes passées par ce programme sont aujourd'hui à la tête d'une région. L’article Économie russe : sous pression budgétaire, les régions réduisent les indemnités versées aux familles des soldats morts en Ukraine est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: ‘PUBG-linked’ bank robber arrested from home in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: The police claim to have arrested a young man hours after he looted Rs700,000 by getting a “bank robbery task” from the PUBG game at Bhatta Chowk in Defence here on Friday. DIG Operations Faisal Kamran told mediapersons that the robbery took place at around 9:30am near Bhatta Chowk. He said a masked suspect entered the bank premises after taking the guard hostage. He then reached the cash counter, along with the hostage guard, collected cash and escaped the scene. The crime was committed within a few minutes. The DIG said that soon after looting the cash, the suspect drove back to his home which showed that he was not a habitual criminal. DIG says financial difficulties pushed UK-returned youth to commit crime by seeking help from the online game He said police teams were formed soon after receiving an emergency 15 call about the robbery, adding that the police traced him through the Safe City and private cameras and reached his house, located a few minutes’ drive away from the bank. The DIG said that the suspect was identified as Subhan, who had returned to Pakistan from the UK on Sept 16. He said the suspect was living alone in Lahore as his family was settled in the UK. He said that the suspect had been playing the PUBG game for the last many years. On the day of the incident, he got a ‘task’ from the game to rob a bank and acquired a mask and a pistol from somewhere to execute the crime. He said the police interrogated the suspect when he talked about the game, keeping in view such incidents in the past involving young men. He said that the arrested suspect also briefed the police about the methods described in the game to carry out a bank robbery. The DIG said that the suspect was planning to flee to Islamabad with the looted money when the police raided the house. He said the weapon, looted cash and a briefcase were recovered from him. He said that the suspect had changed his vehicle’s number plates to mislead the police. The DIG said the suspect had £1,200 when he reached Pakistan, however, he spent the entire amount and had been demanding more money from his family. When his family refused, he planned the bank robbery to overcome his financial constraints, he added. He said that according to initial investigations, he was influenced by online gaming and web series. Published in Dawn, October 3rd, 2026

items.title: Five shop owners move court to include terrorism, murder charges in Gul Plaza fire case
items.description: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Friday issued notices for Saturday (today) to members of Gul Plaza Management Committee and the investigating officer (IO) on a petition filed by five shop owners of the mall, seeking to record their statements before the court to include charges of murder and terrorism. Speaking to Dawn , prosecutor Hassan Bhatti said that two applications had been moved by the shop owners before Judicial Magistrate (South) Aasim Aslam. He said the shop owners had already recorded their statements before the IO under Section 161 (examination of witnesses by police) of the criminal procedure code and now they wanted to record their statement before the magistrate. He further stated that the prosecution did not oppose the plea seeking to record their statements before the court. However, he added that the prosecution opposed the plea seeking to include charges of murder and terrorism and treat the incident as the Baldia Factory fire incident. Prosecutor Bhatti told Dawn that he argued before the court that the Gul Plaza fire was a separate incident. He added that in the Baldia Factory fire case, a chemical report had found phosphorus, and there was also an alleged intention behind the incident as the factory owners had not paid the ransom demanded by the accused persons. He added that the Gul Plaza incident was separate and that the fire had broken out unintentionally, as per statements recorded by prosecution witnesses. According to witnesses, he added that a teenage boy was playing with matchsticks, which led to the fire in the mall. Meanwhile, defence counsel Shaikh Jawaid Mir, representing members of the Gul Plaza Management Committee — Tanveer Pasta, Amar Ismail, Muhammad Ramazan and Muhammad Ameen — as well as the owner of an artificial flower shop, Naimatullah, and his over 11-year-old son, Huzaifa, had raised objections to the plea seeking to include murder and terrorism charges in the case. After hearing arguments from all sides, the court issued notices to the suspects and the IO regarding recording of their statements and directed them to appear in person on Saturday (today) for hearing. Regarding the plea seeking to include murder and terrorism charges in the case, the court adjourned the matter until Oct 7. Published in Dawn, October 3rd, 2026

items.title: Ebola en RDC: l'épidémie franchit le seuil des 4000 morts malgré l'optimisme du ministre de la Santé
items.description: L’épidémie d’Ebola a franchi le seuil des 4 000 morts en République démocratique du Congo, pour plus de 8 300 cas confirmés. Le pays fait face à la plus grave flambée de son histoire. Malgré ce bilan particulièrement lourd, les autorités sanitaires congolaises se veulent rassurantes. Lors d’une conférence de presse tenue vendredi à Kinshasa, le ministre de la Santé, Roger Kamba, a affirmé que « le pic est derrière nous ».

items.title: Sánchez mide el alcance del malestar social contra la derecha para decidir si convoca ya elecciones
items.description: Estaba escrita y medida, y la frase lo decía todo: “ Hagan lo correcto porque la historia les juzgará antes de lo que creen y con más contundencia de la que se imaginan” . Al escucharla, buena parte del hemiciclo interpretó en ese “antes de lo que creen” que Pedro Sánchez ya tiene totalmente decidido adelantar las elecciones de manera inminente , en la primera fecha posible, el 29 de noviembre. La realidad, según diversas fuentes del entorno del presidente y personas que hablaron con él en la larga jornada en el Congreso, es que Sánchez aún no ha tomado una decisión definitiva, aunque el adelanto electoral inmediato sí está encima de su mesa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: No más incertidumbre
items.description: Pedro Sánchez sopesa adelantar las elecciones generales, y esta posibilidad electrizó ayer el pleno extraordinario del Congreso en el que la mayoría de derechas formada por PP, Vox y Junts derrotó los dos decretos de medidas urgentes sobre la vivienda. Lo que debía ser un debate sobre las propuestas negociadas por el Gobierno en respuesta al estallido social de la última semana quedó reducido a una confrontación de eslóganes. En una intervención no anunciada, el presidente pronosticó que los partidos que votaron en contra recibirán el castigo de la sociedad “antes de lo que creen y con más contundencia de lo que imaginan”. El líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, respondió fuera del hemiciclo : “Acepto el reto”. Fue un ensayo de campaña electoral, aunque no se haya disuelto el Parlamento ni exista una fecha para la convocatoria a las urnas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pablo Bustinduy: “Las elecciones, cuando sean, van a ser un referéndum sobre la vivienda”
items.description: Pablo Bustinduy (Madrid, 43 años) atiende a EL PAÍS nada más acabar el pleno del Congreso que ha derogado este viernes los dos decretos sobre vivienda. El ministro de Derechos Sociales, encargado de defender en el hemiciclo el texto que recogía la prórroga automática de los contratos de alquiler, se reconoce cansado, después de un trabajo intenso las últimas semanas. Pero cuando responde, no escatima en palabras y deja clara su indignación por el voto en contra de las derechas. “La posición de Junts es un suicidio político”, sostiene. No se pronuncia sobre si el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, debe convocar elecciones, pero advierte de que los comicios serán “un referéndum sobre la vivienda”. Seguir leyendo
